  "content": "<script setup lang=\"ts\">\n// Tabbed shell over the two tier-specific matrix views.\n// Company tab — (subCat × admin). Super-admin-only edits.\n// Product-Line tab — (subCat × productLine) grid. Edits permitted for\n//   super-admins anywhere and for company admins of the row's subCat\n//   (delegation rule from ADR-0001, 2026-06-08 addendum).\n// The active tab persists in the URL hash so deep links survive a reload.\n\ntype Tab = \"company\" | \"productLine\"\n\nexport interface ReviewerRow {\n  id: string\n  tier: Tab\n  subCat: string\n  productLineId: string | null\n  userId: string\n  userEmail: string\n  userName: string | null\n  canEdit: boolean\n}\n\nexport interface ProductLine {\n  id: string\n  labelEn: string\n  labelZh: string\n  sortOrder: number\n}\n\nexport interface Viewer {\n  isSuperAdmin: boolean\n  companySubCats: string[]\n}\n\nconst props = defineProps<{\n  reviewers: ReviewerRow[]\n  productLines: ProductLine[]\n  viewer: Viewer\n}>()\nconst emit = defineEmits<{ (e: \"refresh\"): void }>()\n\nconst { t } = useI18n()\n\nconst route = useRoute()\nconst router = useRouter()\n\nconst initialTab: Tab = route.hash === \"#tab=productLine\" ? \"productLine\" : \"company\"\nconst activeTab = ref<Tab>(initialTab)\n\nwatch(activeTab, (next) => {\n  router.replace({ hash: `#tab=${next}` })\n})\n\n// Provide a Ref<boolean> for the subviews so they don't need to thread\n// the viewer prop themselves. Wrapped as a computed so reactivity follows\n// the prop without an explicit re-broadcast.\nconst viewerIsSuperAdmin = computed(() => props.viewer.isSuperAdmin)\nprovide(\"viewerIsSuperAdmin\", viewerIsSuperAdmin)\n\nconst companyRows = computed(() =>\n  props.reviewers\n    .filter((r) => r.tier === \"company\")\n    .map((r) => ({\n      id: r.id,\n      subCat: r.subCat,\n      userId: r.userId,\n      userEmail: r.userEmail,\n      userName: r.userName,\n      canEdit: r.canEdit,\n    })),\n)\n\nconst productLineRows = computed(() =>\n  props.reviewers\n    .filter((r): r is ReviewerRow & { productLineId: string } =>\n      r.tier === \"productLine\" && r.productLineId !== null,\n    )\n    .map((r) => ({\n      id: r.id,\n      subCat: r.subCat,\n      productLineId: r.productLineId,\n      userId: r.userId,\n      userEmail: r.userEmail,\n      userName: r.userName,\n      canEdit: r.canEdit,\n    })),\n)\n</script>\n\n<template>\n  <div class=\"space-y-4\">\n    <div\n      role=\"tablist\"\n      class=\"inline-flex items-center gap-1 rounded-lg border border-(--color-border) bg-(--color-card) p-1\"\n    >\n      <button\n        type=\"button\"\n        role=\"tab\"\n        :aria-selected=\"activeTab === 'company'\"\n        class=\"rounded-md px-3 py-1.5 text-sm font-medium\"\n        :class=\"\n          activeTab === 'company'\n            ? 'bg-(--color-bg) text-(--color-ink) shadow-sm'\n            : 'text-(--color-ink-muted) hover:text-(--color-ink)'\n        \"\n        @click=\"activeTab = 'company'\"\n      >\n        {{ t(\"admin.reviewers.matrix.tabs.company\") }}\n      </button>\n      <button\n        type=\"button\"\n        role=\"tab\"\n        :aria-selected=\"activeTab === 'productLine'\"\n        class=\"rounded-md px-3 py-1.5 text-sm font-medium\"\n        :class=\"\n          activeTab === 'productLine'\n            ? 'bg-(--color-bg) text-(--color-ink) shadow-sm'\n            : 'text-(--color-ink-muted) hover:text-(--color-ink)'\n        \"\n        @click=\"activeTab = 'productLine'\"\n      >\n        {{ t(\"admin.reviewers.matrix.tabs.productLine\") }}\n      </button>\n    </div>\n\n    <p\n      v-if=\"!viewer.isSuperAdmin\"\n      class=\"text-xs text-(--color-ink-muted)\"\n    >\n      {{ t(\"admin.reviewers.matrix.delegationNote\") }}\n    </p>\n\n    <ReviewerMatrixCompany\n      v-if=\"activeTab === 'company'\"\n      :reviewers=\"companyRows\"\n      @refresh=\"emit('refresh')\"\n    />\n    <ReviewerMatrixProductLine\n      v-else\n      :reviewers=\"productLineRows\"\n      :product-lines=\"productLines\"\n      :viewer-company-sub-cats=\"viewer.companySubCats\"\n      @refresh=\"emit('refresh')\"\n    />\n  </div>\n</template>\n"
}

  "new_string": "const open = ref(false)\nconst tier = ref<Tier>(\"productLine\")\nconst subCat = ref<string>(props.currentSubCat ?? \"\")\nconst productLineId = ref<string>(\"\")\nconst reason = ref(\"\")\nconst busy = ref(false)\nconst error = ref<string | null>(null)\n\n// Product line list is small (4 rows) and seldom changes — fetch once\n// when the dialog opens and reuse the same ref. The endpoint requires a\n// signed-in user, so anonymous trigger taps still work (the dialog gates\n// on its own enclosing auth).\ninterface ProductLine {\n  id: string\n  labelEn: string\n  labelZh: string\n  sortOrder: number\n}\nconst productLines = ref<ProductLine[]>([])\nconst productLinesLoaded = ref(false)\nconst productLinesError = ref<string | null>(null)\n\nasync function ensureProductLines() {\n  if (productLinesLoaded.value) return\n  try {\n    const res = await $fetch(\"/api/internal/product-lines\")\n    productLines.value = res.productLines\n    productLinesLoaded.value = true\n  } catch (err) {\n    console.error(\"[approvals] failed to load product lines\", err)\n    productLinesError.value = t(\"approvals.dialog.productLinesError\")\n  }\n}\n\nwatch(open, (next) => {\n  if (next) {\n    tier.value = \"productLine\"\n    subCat.value = props.currentSubCat ?? \"\"\n    productLineId.value = \"\"\n    reason.value = \"\"\n    error.value = null\n    productLinesError.value = null\n    void ensureProductLines()\n  }\n})\n\n// Clear productLineId on tier change so a stale value can't ride\n// along on a company-tier submit and trip `unexpected_product_line`.\nwatch(tier, (next) => {\n  if (next === \"company\") productLineId.value = \"\"\n})\n\nconst canSubmit = computed(() => {\n  if (busy.value) return false\n  if (subCat.value.length === 0) return false\n  if (tier.value === \"productLine\" && productLineId.value.length === 0) {\n    return false\n  }\n  return true\n})\n\nconst orderedLines = computed(() =>\n  [...productLines.value].sort((a, b) => a.sortOrder - b.sortOrder),\n)\n\nfunction lineLabel(line: ProductLine): string {\n  return locale.value === \"zh\" ? line.labelZh : line.labelEn\n}"

  "content": "<script setup lang=\"ts\">\ndefinePageMeta({\n  middleware: [\"require-auth\", \"require-reviewer\"],\n})\n\nconst { t } = useI18n()\n\n// Load the queue and the product-line list in parallel. The queue itself\n// only carries productLineId; we resolve labels client-side so a single\n// productLines fetch covers any future pages on the same session.\nconst { data, refresh, pending } = await useFetch(\n  \"/api/internal/approvals/list\",\n  {\n    query: { view: \"queue\" },\n    default: () => ({ ok: true, requests: [] }),\n  },\n)\nconst { data: productLinesData } = await useFetch(\n  \"/api/internal/product-lines\",\n  {\n    default: () => ({ ok: true, productLines: [] }),\n  },\n)\n\nconst rows = computed(() => data.value.requests)\nconst productLines = computed(() => productLinesData.value.productLines)\n</script>\n\n<template>\n  <div class=\"px-6 py-8 max-w-5xl mx-auto\">\n    <header class=\"mb-6\">\n      <h1 class=\"font-serif text-3xl tracking-tight text-(--color-ink)\">\n        {{ t(\"admin.approvals.title\") }}\n      </h1>\n      <p class=\"mt-1 text-sm text-(--color-ink-muted)\">\n        {{ t(\"admin.approvals.subtitle\") }}\n      </p>\n    </header>\n\n    <p v-if=\"pending\" class=\"text-sm text-(--color-ink-muted)\">\n      {{ t(\"admin.approvals.loading\") }}\n    </p>\n    <ReviewerQueueTable\n      v-else\n      :rows=\"rows\"\n      :product-lines=\"productLines\"\n      @refresh=\"refresh\"\n    />\n  </div>\n</template>\n"
}

  "content": "<script setup lang=\"ts\">\n// Inline product-line picker that only surfaces when the tier filter is\n// already narrowed to `productLine`. Lives next to OfficialTierPill on the\n// single-row quiet pill rail (locked decision #3). The \"All\" option clears\n// the productLineId narrow but keeps the tier=productLine narrow in place.\n\nconst { t, locale } = useI18n()\nconst { filters, update } = useFilters()\n\ninterface ProductLine {\n  id: string\n  labelEn: string\n  labelZh: string\n  sortOrder: number\n}\n\nconst productLines = ref<ProductLine[]>([])\nconst loaded = ref(false)\n\nasync function load() {\n  if (loaded.value) return\n  try {\n    const res = await $fetch(\"/api/internal/product-lines\")\n    productLines.value = res.productLines\n    loaded.value = true\n  } catch (err) {\n    console.error(\"[filters] failed to load product lines\", err)\n  }\n}\n\nconst visible = computed(() => filters.value.tier === \"productLine\")\n\n// Load lazily — only fetch when the rail actually surfaces.\nwatch(\n  visible,\n  (next) => {\n    if (next) void load()\n  },\n  { immediate: true },\n)\n\nconst active = computed(() => filters.value.productLineId ?? \"all\")\nconst orderedLines = computed(() =>\n  [...productLines.value].sort((a, b) => a.sortOrder - b.sortOrder),\n)\nfunction lineLabel(line: ProductLine): string {\n  return locale.value === \"zh\" ? line.labelZh : line.labelEn\n}\n\nfunction onClick(productLineId: string | undefined) {\n  update({ productLineId })\n}\n</script>\n\n<template>\n  <div\n    v-if=\"visible\"\n    role=\"group\"\n    :aria-label=\"t('filters.productLineLabel')\"\n    class=\"flex flex-wrap gap-1\"\n  >\n    <button\n      type=\"button\"\n      :aria-pressed=\"active === 'all'\"\n      class=\"rounded-full border px-2.5 py-0.5 text-[12px] font-semibold transition\"\n      :class=\"\n        active === 'all'\n          ? 'bg-(--color-ink)/8 text-(--color-ink) border-(--color-ink)/25'\n          : 'border-(--color-border) text-(--color-ink-muted) hover:text-(--color-ink)'\n      \"\n      @click=\"onClick(undefined)\"\n    >\n      {{ t(\"filters.productLine.all\") }}\n    </button>\n    <button\n      v-for=\"line in orderedLines\"\n      :key=\"line.id\"\n      type=\"button\"\n      :aria-pressed=\"active === line.id\"\n      class=\"rounded-full border px-2.5 py-0.5 text-[12px] font-semibold transition\"\n      :class=\"\n        active === line.id\n          ? 'bg-(--color-ink)/8 text-(--color-ink) border-(--color-ink)/25'\n          : 'border-(--color-border) text-(--color-ink-muted) hover:text-(--color-ink)'\n      \"\n      @click=\"onClick(line.id)\"\n    >\n      {{ lineLabel(line) }}\n    </button>\n  </div>\n</template>\n"
}

36	const UNITS: Array<[Intl.RelativeTimeFormatUnit, number]> = [

40	  ["day", 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000],

49	  const rtf = new Intl.RelativeTimeFormat(locale.value, { numeric: "auto" })
50	  for (const [unit, ms] of UNITS) {
51	    const value = Math.trunc(diffMs / ms)
52	    if (Math.abs(value) >= 1) return rtf.format(value, unit)
53	  }
54	  return rtf.format(0, "day")
55	})

  "content": "import * as extensionsRepo from \"~~/server/repositories/extensions\"\nimport { listAllProductLines } from \"~~/server/repositories/productLines\"\nimport * as versionsRepo from \"~~/server/repositories/versions\"\n\n// Detail endpoint adds a resolved `productLineLabel` to the response so\n// the hero badge can render \"Wireless Official\" / \"无线官方\" without a\n// second round-trip. The locale comes from the i18n `accept-locale`\n// header set by @nuxtjs/i18n; we fall back to English when absent.\nexport default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {\n  const query = getQuery(event)\n  const slug = typeof query.slug === \"string\" ? query.slug : null\n  if (!slug) throw createError({ statusCode: 400, statusMessage: \"slug required\" })\n\n  const db = useDb()\n  const ext = await extensionsRepo.findBySlug(db, slug)\n  if (!ext) throw createError({ statusCode: 404, statusMessage: \"not_found\" })\n\n  const [versions, related, productLines] = await Promise.all([\n    versionsRepo.listForExtension(db, ext.id),\n    extensionsRepo.findRelated(db, ext.id, ext.category),\n    ext.productLineId ? listAllProductLines(db) : Promise.resolve([]),\n  ])\n\n  const acceptLang = getRequestHeader(event, \"accept-language\") ?? \"\"\n  const isZh = acceptLang.toLowerCase().startsWith(\"zh\")\n  const productLine = ext.productLineId\n    ? productLines.find((l) => l.id === ext.productLineId)\n    : null\n  const productLineLabel = productLine\n    ? isZh\n      ? productLine.labelZh\n      : productLine.labelEn\n    : null\n\n  return { ext: { ...ext, productLineLabel }, versions, related }\n})\n"
}

1	# ADR-0001: Official-tier approval workflow
2	
3	## Status
4	
5	Accepted — 2026-06-07 (shipped via PR #41 merged as `a392c16`).
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	The product needed a moderation path for elevating a published extension
10	to "Official" status. The shape of the workflow was open along four
11	axes, each with plausible alternatives:
12	
13	1. **What does "category" mean for routing?** The taxonomy already
14	   distinguished `funcCat` (3 top-level enum), `subCat` (text drawn
15	   from `FUNC_TAXONOMY.l1`, 9 leaves), and `deptId` (dotted-path text
16	   PK with descendant matching). Any one could plausibly drive the
17	   reviewer matrix.
18	2. **Are the two official tiers (Product-Line and Company) ordered?**
19	   A hierarchical ladder (PL first, then Company) reads naturally as
20	   "earn trust then escalate." Independent tiers let a publisher
21	   apply directly for Company without a PL gate.
22	3. **How does the existing `extensions.badge` column (already
23	   carrying `"official" | "popular" | "new"` and surfaced through the
24	   frozen `/api/v1` contract) interact with the new tier?** Reusing
25	   `badge` keeps the schema small; introducing a new column keeps the
26	   semantics clean.
27	4. **Who can edit the (tier × category) reviewer matrix?** Any
28	   `role='admin'` membership is the lightest model; a separate
29	   super-admin role is a smaller trust circle.
30	
31	The CLI's `/api/v1` shape is frozen (see `docs/plan.md` §13 and
32	`docs/api.md`), so any choice that changed the public response was a
33	contract break and a much larger lift than the workflow needed.
34	
35	## Decision
36	
37	Four locked decisions, taken together:
38	
39	1. **Category = `subCat`** (the FUNC_TAXONOMY l1 leaf). The matrix is
40	   `9 subCats × 2 tiers = 18` cells — concrete enough to assign
41	   without sprawl, fine-grained enough that a network specialist
42	   isn't asked to review documentation tooling.
43	
44	2. **Tiers are independent, not hierarchical.** A publisher picks
45	   their target tier at submission time; Company supersedes
46	   Product-Line if both end up granted on the same extension. The
47	   orchestrator does not require a prior Product-Line approval before
48	   a Company request.
49	
50	3. **`officialTier` is its own enum column.** `extensions.badge`
51	   stays in the DB unchanged. The `/api/v1/extensions/*` mappers
52	   *derive* `badge: "official"` from `officialTier != null` at the
53	   response boundary, so the frozen contract is preserved without a
54	   v2 bump and the CLI sees no change. App code stops writing `badge`
55	   entirely; future removal can ride an intentional v2 break.
56	
57	4. **Matrix admin = `superAdmin` membership role only.** A new value
58	   is appended to `membershipRoleEnum` alongside `viewer | publisher |
59	   admin`. Reviewers decide their own assigned cells; matrix edits
60	   are a separate, smaller trust circle. Super-admins also bypass the
61	   cell-assignment check when deciding (so they can unblock a stuck
62	   request without first assigning themselves).
63	
64	## Consequences
65	
66	What this makes easier:
67	
68	- The reviewer queue ranks naturally by cell and is small enough that
69	  super-admins can hold the whole matrix in their head.
70	- The CLI keeps working without any contract change — useful since
71	  the CLI is distributed via npm and slow to roll forward.
72	- The state machine is small enough to fit in
73	  `shared/approvals/state.ts` as pure functions with full unit
74	  coverage; the orchestrator (`server/utils/approvals.ts`) does
75	  nothing tricky beyond optimistic-lock race detection.
76	
77	What we gave up:
78	
79	- A single "officially endorsed" enum on `extensions` would have been
80	  one fewer column. The separate `officialTier` means we now have
81	  two fields tracking related concepts; the derive-in-mapper
82	  bridges them but is technically duplication.
83	- The independent-tier model lets a brand-new extension apply for
84	  Company on day one. If we later want to require Product-Line
85	  approval as a prerequisite, that's a state-machine change we'd
86	  need a new ADR for.
87	- A `superAdmin` role concentrates matrix-edit authority in one
88	  account by default. Production deployments need to remember to
89	  seed at least one super-admin (`SEED_SUPER_ADMIN_EMAIL`); without
90	  one, the matrix is unmanageable.
91	
92	Open follow-ups (not blocking):
93	
94	- **Tier revocation** — a super-admin removing a granted tier is not
95	  yet supported. Data model allows `null` already; needs a single
96	  orchestrator + endpoint.
97	- **Notification fan-out** — the orchestrator emits
98	  `extension/approval.{requested,decided}` Inngest events, but the
99	  current consumer only logs them. Email / in-app notifications are
100	  P1.
101	- **Audit trail for matrix edits** — today we record the decision +
102	  note on each request row but don't capture super-admin matrix
103	  changes. If audit becomes a requirement, add a dedicated
104	  `audit_events` table in a follow-up ADR.
105	
106	## Cross-references
107	
108	- Schema: `shared/db/schema/approval.ts`, `shared/db/schema/extension.ts`
109	- Pure decisions: `shared/approvals/state.ts`
110	- Orchestrator: `server/utils/approvals.ts`
111	- Public-contract bridge: `server/api/v1/extensions/index.get.ts:36`
112	  and `server/api/v1/extensions/[slug]/index.get.ts:24`
113	- CLAUDE.md decision #12 (summary entry pointing here)
114	- `docs/plan.md` §3 (schema additions) and `P21` status entry
115

  "new_string": "## Cross-references\n\n- Schema: `shared/db/schema/approval.ts`, `shared/db/schema/extension.ts`\n- Pure decisions: `shared/approvals/state.ts`\n- Orchestrator: `server/utils/approvals.ts`\n- Public-contract bridge: `server/api/v1/extensions/index.get.ts:36`\n  and `server/api/v1/extensions/[slug]/index.get.ts:24`\n- CLAUDE.md decision #12 (summary entry pointing here)\n- `docs/plan.md` §3 (schema additions) and `P21` status entry\n\n## Update 2026-06-08 — product-line dimension\n\nPR #41's matrix routed exclusively on `(tier × subCat)`. Reality at\nNaive is that the company is organised in **multiple product lines**\n(Wireless, Datacom, Terminals, Cloud), and each functional category\ninside each product line wants its own admin. The original matrix\ncollapses all four lines onto one cell per subCat, which is the wrong\nunit of trust — a Wireless network specialist isn't the right reviewer\nfor a Cloud network skill. The Product-Line tier therefore needs a\nthird axis. The Company tier stays one admin per subCat — that level\nis intentionally cross-line.\n\nA second constraint surfaced at the same time: the company-tier admin\nof a given subCat is the right person to **pick the product-line\nadmins** for that same subCat. The original `superAdmin`-only gate\nmakes them ask a super-admin every time, which doesn't scale and\ndoesn't reflect the org chart.\n\nRefinements (do not revoke the original four locked decisions; they\nremain accurate):\n\n- **Decision #1 refines**: routing key is `(tier × subCat × productLine?)`,\n  where `productLine` is required iff `tier='productLine'` and absent\n  otherwise. The reviewer matrix table widens to\n  `9 subCats × 1 Company + 9 subCats × 4 ProductLines = 45` cells.\n  `productLines` is a seeded lookup table (id, label_en, label_zh,\n  sort_order), kept as data rather than a code enum so adding a line\n  is a content migration. CHECK constraints on\n  `approval_reviewers`, `approval_requests`, and `extensions` enforce\n  the iff-rule at the boundary — repository and orchestrator code can\n  rely on it as a hard backstop.\n- **Decision #4 widens**: matrix edits remain super-admin-able anywhere,\n  but a **company-tier admin of subCat X may now manage productLine\n  cells of subCat X (any productLine)**. Company-tier cells stay\n  super-admin-only. The new `requireCellAdmin(event, cell)` helper\n  encodes the rule; `unassign.delete.ts` loads the target row first so\n  the gate authorises against the row's own coordinates rather than\n  the caller's request body.\n\nImplementation notes:\n\n- **Partial unique indexes over `NULLS NOT DISTINCT`** on\n  `approval_reviewers`: two indexes, one per tier, each carrying\n  exactly the columns that participate. This is clearer than one\n  unique index with quirky NULL semantics and lets each tier's arity\n  stand on its own in `\\d`.\n- **`/api/v1` contract is unchanged.** `badge: ext.officialTier\n  ? \"official\" : ext.badge` already collapses tier away; productLineId\n  is intentionally suppressed at the same boundary. A future v2 break\n  could expose the tier + line; until then the CLI sees nothing new.\n- **`listReviewerQueue` dedup key** picks `productLineId ?? '∅'` for\n  the super-admin fan-out so a `(company, cloud, null)` cell can't\n  collide with `(productLine, cloud, '')` in the Set.\n\nWhat this gives up:\n\n- Single product line per extension. Multi-line endorsement would\n  require a `extension_official_product_lines` join table and is\n  rejected for v1 as additional surface area for a use case nobody has\n  asked for. A publisher who wants two endorsements submits two\n  separate requests; the latest approved one stamps the extension.\n- A non-super company admin can still grow the productLine reviewer\n  pool unbounded inside their subCat. We accept this — the trust\n  circle for \"your own subCat\" is small by construction.\n\nCross-references for this update:\n\n- Migration: `drizzle/0009_last_naoko.sql`\n- New helpers: `server/utils/auth.ts` (`requireCellAdmin`),\n  `server/repositories/reviewers.ts` (`isCompanyAdminForSubCat`,\n  `listCompanySubCatsForUser`, `findReviewerById`).\n- New repo: `server/repositories/productLines.ts`\n- New endpoint: `server/api/internal/product-lines/index.get.ts`\n- UI: `app/components/approvals/ReviewerMatrix{,Company,ProductLine}.vue`,\n  `app/components/approvals/RequestOfficialDialog.vue`,\n  `app/components/filters/ProductLinePill.vue`, and the\n  `extensions.officialTier.productLineWith` i18n key consumed by\n  `app/components/extension/ExtHero.vue`."
}

230	
231	- Department descendant matching uses the dotted-path id directly: `WHERE deptId = $1 OR deptId LIKE $1 || '.%'`. This requires `text_pattern_ops` on `deptId` to use the index for `LIKE`. No recursive CTE.
232	- `(funcCat, subCat, l2)` covers drill-down.
233	- Sort indexes are separate (`downloadsCount DESC`, `starsAvg DESC`).
234	
235	### Additions for the approval workflow (shipped in PR #41)
236	
237	The approval workflow added three load-bearing pieces — see
238	`shared/db/schema/extension.ts`, `shared/db/schema/org.ts`, and
239	`shared/db/schema/approval.ts` for the canonical definitions, and
240	`docs/adr/0001-official-tier-approval-workflow.md` for the rationale.
241	
242	- **`extensions.officialTier`** — nullable `extension_official_tier` enum
243	  (`productLine | company`). Null = "Unofficial" (the default for any
244	  publisher-uploaded extension). The existing `badge` column is
245	  preserved; the `/api/v1/extensions/*` mappers derive `badge:
246	  "official"` from `officialTier != null` so the frozen CLI shape is
247	  unchanged. App code only writes `officialTier`. Indexed as
248	  `idx_ext_official_tier`.
249	- **`memberships.role`** — the `membership_role` enum gains a
250	  `superAdmin` value alongside `viewer | publisher | admin`. The
251	  migration uses `ALTER TYPE … ADD VALUE`; safe inside the same
252	  transaction on PG12+ because the new value is never referenced in
253	  the same migration.
254	- **`approval_requests`** — one row per submitted elevation request.
255	  Columns: id, extensionId (FK CASCADE), requestedTier
256	  (`extension_official_tier`), snapshotted subCat (text, validated
257	  against `FUNC_TAXONOMY` l1 leaves at the orchestrator), requestedBy
258	  user, reason, status (`approval_status` enum: pending | approved |
259	  rejected | withdrawn), decidedBy user, decidedAt, reviewerNote,
260	  timestamps. Indexes: `(status, subCat, requestedTier)` for the
261	  reviewer queue; `(extensionId, status)` for the publisher view and
262	  the at-most-one-pending guard the orchestrator enforces inside the
263	  insert's transaction.
264	- **`approval_reviewers`** — the configurable (tier × subCat) → user
265	  matrix. Multiple reviewers per cell; first decision wins. Unique
266	  on `(tier, subCat, userId)` to make `onConflictDoNothing` work.
267	  Indexed on `(tier, subCat)` for fan-out lookups.
268	
269	The complete shape sits in `drizzle/0008_large_lizard.sql`.

Multiple reviewers per cell; first decision wins. Unique\n  on `(tier, subCat, userId)` to make `onConflictDoNothing` work.\n  Indexed on `(tier, subCat)` for fan-out lookups.\n\nThe complete shape sits in `drizzle/0008_large_lizard.sql`.",

Null = \"Unofficial\" (the default for any\n  publisher-uploaded extension). The existing `badge` column is\n  preserved; the `/api/v1/extensions/*` mappers derive `badge:\n  \"official\"` from `officialTier != null` so the frozen CLI shape is\n  unchanged. App code only writes `officialTier`. Indexed as\n  `idx_ext_official_tier`.\n- **`extensions.productLineId`** — nullable FK to `product_lines.id`.\n  Required iff `officialTier='productLine'` (a CHECK constraint\n  enforces the iff-rule). `ON DELETE SET NULL` so retiring a product\n  line doesn't orphan extension rows.\n- **`product_lines`** — seeded lookup table for the new dimension:\n  `id` (kebab-case text PK), `label_en`, `label_zh`, `sort_order`,\n  `created_at`. Seeded by `0009_*` with `wireless`, `datacom`,\n  `terminals`, `cloud`; adding a line is a content migration, not a\n  code release.\n- **`memberships.role`** — the `membership_role` enum gains a\n  `superAdmin` value alongside `viewer | publisher | admin`. The\n  migration uses `ALTER TYPE … ADD VALUE`; safe inside the same\n  transaction on PG12+ because the new value is never referenced in\n  the same migration.\n- **`approval_requests`** — one row per submitted elevation request.\n  Columns: id, extensionId (FK CASCADE), requestedTier\n  (`extension_official_tier`), snapshotted subCat (text, validated\n  against `FUNC_TAXONOMY` l1 leaves at the orchestrator),\n  productLineId (text FK to `product_lines.id`, present iff\n  `requestedTier='productLine'`), requestedBy user, reason, status\n  (`approval_status` enum: pending | approved | rejected | withdrawn),\n  decidedBy user, decidedAt, reviewerNote, timestamps. Indexes:\n  `(status, subCat, requestedTier, productLineId)` for the reviewer\n  queue; `(extensionId, status)` for the publisher view and the\n  at-most-one-pending guard the orchestrator enforces inside the\n  insert's transaction. A CHECK enforces the productLineId iff-rule.\n- **`approval_reviewers`** — the configurable\n  `(tier × subCat × productLineId?)` → user matrix. Multiple reviewers\n  per cell; first decision wins. **Two partial unique indexes** —\n  `(tier, sub_cat, product_line_id, user_id) WHERE tier='productLine'`\n  and `(tier, sub_cat, user_id) WHERE tier='company'` — express the\n  different per-tier arities self-documentingly; preferred over\n  `NULLS NOT DISTINCT`. CHECK enforces the iff-rule.\n\nThe original shape shipped in `drizzle/0008_large_lizard.sql`; the\nproduct-line dimension is in `drizzle/0009_last_naoko.sql`."

# AgentCenter Feature Inventory · 功能清单

Source-of-truth list of what's shipped today, organized by capability area. For what changed when, see [daily-log.md](./daily-log.md).

当前已交付的能力清单，按功能领域分组。每日变更记录见 [daily-log.md](./daily-log.md)。

---

## English

**Overview.** A bilingual marketplace for AI agent extensions (Skills, MCP servers, slash commands, plugins). Users can browse and search a catalog with rich filters, view detail pages with READMEs and stats, publish their own extensions through a 4-step wizard with automated bundle scanning, save favorites, and authorize a CLI for installs. Open sign-up, EN/ZH UI and content, themes, and a public registry API. Multi-tenant schema with a single-tenant UI in v1.

### Browse & discover

- **Type-first browsing** — Browsing the marketplace starts by picking a type — Skills, MCP Servers, Slash Commands, or Plugins — from the Explore dropdown in the top bar. The unfiltered catalog stays reachable but isn't the default destination.
- **Function-types sidebar** — A persistent sidebar tree exposes the three-level functional taxonomy (Work Task / Business / Tools, plus sub-categories and leaves). Selecting any node filters the catalog and survives URL sharing.
- **Extension catalog** — Browse all published extensions in a paginated grid at `/extensions`.
- **Search** — Search by any phrase, in English or Chinese, including short fragments.
- **Department picker** — Narrow to a department and all of its sub-departments.
- **Scope filter** — Filter by Personal, Organization, or Enterprise.
- **Tag filters** — Multi-select tags with "any" or "all" matching.
- **Sort** — Sort by downloads, stars, or most recently updated.
- **Creator filter** — Filter by the user who published the extension.
- **Publisher filter** — Filter by the organization behind the extension.
- **Shareable filter state** — Every filter combination is reflected in the URL, so any search can be bookmarked or shared.
- **Active-filter chips** — Above the results grid, each applied filter (search term, scope, department, creator, publisher, every selected tag) renders as a removable chip — click × to drop one, or "Clear all" to clear them in a single tap.
- **Home: featured spotlight** — A curated "Featured this week" extension anchors the home page with its name, tagline, install command, and a deep link to the detail page; falls back to a slim editorial card when no extension is marked featured.
- **Home: trending row** — A cross-category mix of trending extensions (Skills, MCP servers, slash commands, plugins).
- **Whole-card click** — Click anywhere on an extension card to open it; Save / Install stay independently clickable.

11	---

14	
15	### 2026-05-21
16	
17	**Briefing.** Today's release brings an editorial pass to the extension list and detail pages — cards simplify into preview rectangles with a single meta line, the filter rail collapses to a quiet single row with dismissible state chips, the detail-page hero gains a stronger anchor and a confident primary CTA, and every tab body now sits inside its own framed card.
18	
19	<details>
20	<summary>Details</summary>
21	
22	- **A simpler extension card** — Cards on the browse page drop the tag pills and the inline Install button. Each one now reads as a preview rectangle: a slightly larger icon, name + badge, a three-line description, and a single meta line carrying department, star rating, and download count. Clicking anywhere on the card opens the detail page where install lives. (#27)
23	
24	- **A quieter filter rail** — The browse filters collapse from three rows to a single line of compact pills. The hard divider beneath them is gone; active states are subtly tinted rather than ink-inverted; the "Scope:", "Department:", "Creator:", and "Publisher:" labels drop because the controls speak for themselves. The redundant Trending / New / Official / Open Source quick-filter row goes away — sort and the visible Official badge already cover the same ground. (#27)
25	
26	- **You can see and dismiss what's filtered** — A new strip between the filters and the grid shows the result count plus a chip for each active filter (search term, scope, department, creator, publisher, each selected tag); click the × to remove just that filter, or "Clear all" to drop them in one tap. The sort control moves to this strip too, where it logically belongs next to the count. (#27)
27	
28	- **Placeholder cards while results load** — First paint now shows eight subtle skeleton tiles in the grid rather than a blank space. (#27)
29	
30	- **A breadcrumb back to the list** — A small "← Browse extensions" link sits above every detail page, so deep-linked detail views have a clear way back without relying on browser history. (#27)
31	
32	- **A more confident detail hero** — Title shifts to a larger serif, description reads as a lede with more leading, the icon grows, and the stats line uses proper middle-dot separators. The Install button is now the page's clear primary action — larger, accent-filled — with Save and Share matching it in size but staying neutral. (#27)
33	
34	- **README and tab bodies in framed cards** — Overview, Setup, and Permissions each render inside their own bordered card matching the sidebar, so the main content reads with the same composed weight as the rest of the page. (#27)
35	
36	- **An editorial sidebar** — The About and Related panels gain serif headers, more breathing room, and refined typography. Related entries now show a badge, the owning department, and a star rating beside each name, so the recommendations feel like recommendations rather than an afterthought. (#27)
37	
38	- **Underline-on-active tabs** — Overview / Setup / Permissions switch from a subtle background swap to a clean ink underline beneath the active tab, making the current section unambiguous. (#27)
39	
40	- **Robust on narrow viewports and missing data** — The browse grid collapses to a single column below 640px wide instead of overflowing, the star rating displays nothing rather than "NaN" when an extension has no ratings yet, and Official / Popular / New badges now render in Chinese on `/zh` pages. (#27)
41	
42	</details>
43	
44	---
45	
46	### 2026-05-19
47	
48	**Briefing.** Today's release reshapes the MCP Panorama around realistic multi-MCP tools — a software tool can now expose several MCP servers — and strips editorial labels from every group's stats in favour of the raw numbers, all of which double as one-click drill and filter actions.
49	
50	<details>
51	<summary>Details</summary>
52	
53	- **A software tool can ship multiple MCPs** — A tool no longer collapses to one MCP listing. CodeCheck now exposes both codecheck-mcp and molint-mcp; K8sOps and ObservHub each ship three. The detail panel adds an "Other MCPs in this tool" switcher so you can jump between sibling MCPs without closing the panel. (#24)
54	
55	- **A more realistic MCP inventory** — Every MCP carries a descriptive name (kubectl-mcp, helm-mcp, metrics-mcp, identity-mcp, …) instead of a generic "tool-name-mcp" placeholder. The pool of "no MCP needed" tools shrinks from 19 to 6 truly legacy or manual workflows, so the panorama reflects an organization that actually ships MCPs. (#24)
56	
57	- **Tool-as-card layout** — Each software tool reads as a small quiet card with a serif name and a small status dot; its MCP servers render inside as vivid status-coloured pills. PDTs become subtly recessed regions, giving the page a clear hierarchy: domain → recessed PDT → raised tool card → vivid MCP pills. (#24)
58	
59	- **Raw numbers replace ranking labels** — Group headers no longer carry a "Leading / On track / Lagging" verdict pill. Each shows the underlying numbers — total count, a "5/8 released" fraction, and a thin stacked status bar. The summary's right block lists the top three groups by release %, ranked numerically, instead of singling out one "Leading" name. (#25)

── app/components/approvals/ReviewerMatrix.vue:51 ──
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Route hash changes from browser navigation won't update the active tab.**

The component reads `route.hash` once during setup (line 46) and watches `activeTab` to update the hash (lines 49-51), but there's no reverse binding. If a user navigates with browser back/forward buttons, the hash will change but `activeTab` won't react, leaving the UI out of sync with the URL.





<details>
<summary>🔄 Recommended fix to sync activeTab when route.hash changes</summary>

Add a watcher for route.hash to update activeTab:

```diff
 watch(activeTab, (next) => {
   router.replace({ hash: `#tab=${next}` })
 })
+
+watch(
+  () => route.hash,
+  (newHash) => {
+    const tab: Tab = newHash === "`#tab`=productLine" ? "productLine" : "company"
+    if (activeTab.value !== tab) {
+      activeTab.value = tab
+    }
+  },
+)
```

</details>

<!-- suggestion_start -->

<details>
<summary>📝 Committable suggestion</summary>

> ‼️ **IMPORTANT**
> Carefully review the code before committing. Ensure that it accurately replaces the highlighted code, contains no missing lines, and has no issues with indentation. Thoroughly test & benchmark the code to ensure it meets the requirements.

```suggestion
const initialTab: Tab = route.hash === "`#tab`=productLine" ? "productLine" : "company"
const activeTab = ref<Tab>(initialTab)

watch(activeTab, (next) => {
  router.replace({ hash: `#tab=${next}` })
})

watch(
  () => route.hash,
  (newHash) => {
    const tab: Tab = newHash === "`#tab`=productLine" ? "productLine" : "company"
    if (activeTab.value !== tab) {
      activeTab.value = tab
    }
  },
)
```

</details>

In `@nuxtjs/i18n` v10, server-side locale detection is primarily handled through a centralized, experimental locale detector mechanism that executes on the Nitro server [1][2][3]. ### Locale Detection on the Server To perform server-side locale detection, you must define a locale detector function using the defineI18nLocaleDetector composable [1][4]. This function is called on every server request, allowing you to prioritize sources like query parameters, cookies, and HTTP headers [1][3][4]. You must register this detector in your nuxt.config by providing the file path to the experimental.localeDetector option [1][3][4]. Example detector configuration: // localeDetector.ts export default defineI18nLocaleDetector((event, config) => { // 1. Try query parameter const query = tryQueryLocale(event, { lang: '' }) if (query) return query.toString // 2. Try cookie const cookie = tryCookieLocale(event, { lang: '', name: 'i18n_locale' }) if (cookie) return cookie.toString // 3. Try accept-language header const header = tryHeaderLocale(event, { lang: '' }) if (header) return header.toString // 4. Fallback return config.defaultLocale }) ### Handling accept-language Headers The utility tryHeaderLocale(event) is the standard method for extracting the locale from the accept-language header on the server side [1][4]. This utility is designed to be used within the locale detector to automatically match header-provided languages against your configured locales [1][5]. ### Server-Side Locale Access Accessing the resolved locale or translation functions on the server depends on your specific use case: 1. Server-Side Translations: Use the useTranslation(event) composable within Nitro event handlers to perform translations directly on the server [1][4][6]. 2. Redirection and Context: The module now handles localized redirection at the Nitro server level [2][7]. While you generally do not need to manually manage the locale state in Nitro events, internal state is tracked via the request event context [7][8][9]. 3. Client-Side Synchronization: v10 improves efficiency by reusing server-detected locales on the client, preventing redundant detection logic during the initial page load [8]. Note: For standard browser language detection (where you want the module to automatically handle redirects based on user settings), use the detectBrowserLanguage option [3][5]. This is generally preferred over manual implementation unless you require custom server-side logic [5].

- `0009` backfill sentinel: codebase is pre-prod, no real legacy data.

Found it. The endpoint requires authentication (`requireUser`), but the listing page filter rail is shown to anonymous browsers. The fetch 401s, the `catch` block silently swallows it, `productLines.value` stays `[]`, and only the unconditional "All lines" button renders.

The product-line list is non-sensitive reference data (it's the same labels CodeRabbit was happy to see in the catalog). Removing the gate is the right call.

> AGENT

Fixed and pushed (`f673a54`).

**Cause**: the `/api/internal/product-lines` endpoint had `await requireUser(event)`. When you browsed anonymously, the fetch 401d, the `ProductLinePill`'s `catch` silently swallowed it, and `productLines.value` stayed empty — so only the unconditional "All lines" button rendered.

**Fix**: dropped the auth gate. The list is non-sensitive (it's the same labels every productLine-tier badge already shows on every detail page).

Try again after the deploy — picking Product-Line should now show Wireless / Datacom / Terminals / Cloud as clickable pills.

The DB hasn't picked up the new migration — `product_lines` doesn't exist on your local Postgres yet. The schema/seed are correct; you just need to apply `0009_*` (and `0010_*`).

Run:

```
bun run db:migrate
```

That applies both new migrations:
- `0009_last_naoko.sql` — creates the `product_lines` table and seeds Wireless / Datacom / Terminals / Cloud, plus adds `productLineId` to `extensions`, `approval_reviewers`, `approval_requests` with the CHECK + partial unique indexes.
- `0010_early_vargas.sql` — flips the `extensions.productLineId` FK to `ON DELETE RESTRICT` (from the review feedback).

After it finishes, the `/api/internal/product-lines` request will return the four rows and the pill rail will populate. The dev server's HMR should pick it up without restart, but if not, ctrl-C and relaunch with `bun dev`.

If you also want the demo seed updated with the new productLine-fanned-out reviewer matrix and the catalog's per-entry product lines, re-run:

```
bun run db:seed
```

(safe — the seed truncates and re-inserts).

### 5. **Worst-Case Visual Count (tier=productLine active)**

When a user selects `tier=productLine`, on a typical desktop viewport:

**On the single FilterBar row (before wrapping):**
- ScopePills: 4 buttons
- OfficialTierPill: 4 buttons
- ProductLinePill (now visible): ~8 buttons (1 "All lines" + ~7 product lines, depending on API response)
- DeptPicker trigger: 1 button
- CreatorPicker trigger: 1 button (if creators data exists)
- PublisherPicker trigger: 1 button (if publishers data exists)
- TagDrawer trigger: 1 button (if tags data exists)

**Total interactive buttons on single row: ~20–22 elements**

**Wrapping behavior:**
- The `flex-wrap` on FilterBar allows wrapping; with ProductLinePill visible, typical width (even on 1440px+ viewports) will cause the row to break into 2–3 lines depending on browser font rendering and device pixel density
- TagDrawer panel (when expanded) has `basis-full mt-1` (line 75 of TagDrawer.vue), so it explicitly wraps to a new row below the pills

**No horizontal scroll; no "More" or overflow menu currently exists on the filter rail itself.**

### 6. **TagDrawer Behavior (drawer panel wrapping)**

**File:** `TagDrawer.vue` (lines 49–142)

- **Trigger:** Inline button (line 50), stays on the pill rail
- **Panel behavior:** When `open = true`, a new `div` with `class="basis-full mt-1 rounded-md border ... p-3"` (line 75) renders below the trigger, forcing a new row
- **Panel content:** Flex-wrapped tag buttons (lines 77–91), with "Show more/less" toggle (lines 93–100), and optional match-mode selector + clear button (lines 103–139)
- **Closing:** Panel collapses on `open = false`; no automatic dismiss on selection (selections are multi, not terminal)

---

### 8. **Existing Overflow/Drawer Patterns Reusable**

**Reka UI Primitives (already wired in `app/components/ui/`):**
- `Popover.vue`, `PopoverTrigger.vue`, `PopoverContent.vue` — Used by DeptPicker, CreatorPicker, PublisherPicker
- `Select.vue`, `SelectContent.vue`, `SelectTrigger.vue`, `SelectItem.vue` — Generic Reka select; available but not used in filter rail
- `Sheet.vue`, `SheetContent.vue` (drawer/modal) — Not currently used in filter rail

**Pattern precedent in codebase:**
- **TagDrawer's `basis-full` expand pattern** — Trigger stays inline; panel wraps below via Tailwind's `basis-full` utility
- **HomeTagRail.vue (lines 19–34)** — Uses horizontal `overflow-x-auto` for tag rail; shows top 8 tags by count, not a "more" dropdown
- **SelectContent.vue (line 33)** — Uses `max-h-96 overflow-y-auto` for dropdown content; available as a reusable pattern

**No existing "More" button / collapsed-group UI component** currently used anywhere in the extension listing filter rail. TagDrawer's `showMoreCount` toggle (with "+{count} more" text) is the closest pattern, but it only controls visibility within the drawer's expanded panel, not a popover.

---

### Summary for Streamlining

The rail is currently a **single flex-wrap row** that breaks into **2–3 physical lines** at typical viewport widths when ProductLinePill is visible. The 20+ buttons are not hidden behind any overflow control; they're all rendered to the DOM. The rail feels cluttered because:

1. ProductLinePill adds 7–11 visible buttons whenever `tier=productLine` is selected
2. All 7 child components (including 3 popover pickers) mount simultaneously with no conditional collapse
3. TagDrawer panel opens inline (basis-full), creating a separate visual layer
4. No "More" or grouping pattern exists; every option is equally prominent

The codebase has `Popover` (Reka UI) and `Sheet` primitives available for potential UI restructuring, and the `showMoreCount` + toggle pattern from TagDrawer shows precedent for collapsible option groups.
```

The two inline pill groups (Scope/Tier/ProductLine) compete visually and use a different affordance than the popover-trigger pickers (Dept/Creator/Publisher/Tags) — so the rail reads as two languages stacked together.

## Approved Plan:
# Plan: Streamline the listing-page filter rail

## Context

The product-line dimension shipped in PR #43 made an existing visual problem worse: when a user picks `tier=productLine`, the filter rail mounts **~20 interactive elements** on one row (4 Scope pills + 4 Tier pills + 5 Product-Line pills + 4 picker triggers for Dept/Creator/Publisher/Tags), wrapping into 2–3 physical lines on a typical viewport. The rail also mixes two affordances — inline pill rails (Scope/Tier/ProductLine) next to popover-trigger pills (Dept/Creator/Publisher/Tags) — so it reads as two visual languages stacked together.

Locked decision #3 (CLAUDE.md) prescribes "a single-row quiet pill rail" with **Scope pills inline + Dept/Creator/Publisher pickers + Tag-drawer trigger**. The tier/product-line pills were added later in the inline-pill style; they aren't in the locked decision and aren't load-bearing as inline rails. Collapsing them into one Official picker gets the rail back to a single row that honours decision #3 with no breaking changes.

User decisions captured upstream:
1. **Collapse Tier + Product Line into one picker, keep Scope inline.** Scope stays the only inline pill group per locked decision #3.
2. **Picker trigger reads "Dimension: Value"** (e.g. "Official: Wireless", "Official: All"), matching the existing CreatorPicker / PublisherPicker / DeptPicker label convention.

## Target outcome

```
[All] [Personal] [Org] [Enterprise]   [Official: Wireless ▾] [Department ▾] [Creator ▾] [Publisher ▾] [Tags ▾]
```

9 elements on the row (down from ~20), single row at typical viewport widths, no URL contract change (`?tier=productLine&productLineId=wireless` still works), no API change.

## Behaviour spec for `OfficialTierPicker`

A single popover trigger that owns both the `tier` and `productLineId` filter keys.

**Trigger label** — computed from `filters.tier` and `filters.productLineId`:

| State | Label |
| --- | --- |
| `tier=undefined` | `Official: All` (muted, idle style) |
| `tier=unofficial` | `Official: Unofficial` (active style) |
| `tier=company` | `Official: Company` (active style) |
| `tier=productLine`, no productLineId | `Official: Product-Line` (active style) |
| `tier=productLine`, productLineId=X | `Official: {{ lineLabel(X) }}` (active style) — e.g. "Official: Wireless" |

Truncate at `max-w-[140px]` like CreatorPicker.

**Popover content** — two stacked sections:

1. **Tier** section — small header (`filters.tier.tierSection`, "Tier"), then a row of 4 inline option buttons (All / Unofficial / Product-Line / Company). Active state matches the existing inline pills. Clicking a tier:
   - updates `filters.tier` to the picked value (`undefined` for "All")
   - if the new tier is **not** `productLine`, clears `filters.productLineId` in the *same* `update({...})` call so the URL never carries a stale productLineId on a non-productLine tier (mirrors the iff-rule the validator/server already enforce)
   - leaves the popover open so the user can continue into the product-line row

2. **Product line** section — appears only when `filters.tier === "productLine"`. Same small header (`filters.productLine.lineSection`, "Product line"), then a row of N+1 inline buttons (All lines + one per fetched product line). Clicking a line updates `filters.productLineId`. Popover stays open.

**Outside click / Escape** closes the popover (Reka UI default).

**Data load** — same lazy-load pattern as today's `ProductLinePill`: `useState`-cached `$fetch("/api/internal/product-lines")` fired the first time the popover opens *and* when `tier=productLine` is the initial URL state. The endpoint is already anon-accessible after the fix in `f673a54`.

## Files to change

### Add
- `app/components/filters/OfficialTierPicker.vue` — new component. Mirror the structure of `app/components/filters/CreatorPicker.vue:30-75` (Popover + PopoverTrigger with ChevronDown + truncated label + PopoverContent with `align="start"` and `w-[280px] p-0` styling). Two stacked option rows inside.

### Modify
- `app/components/filters/FilterBar.vue:11-21` — replace `<OfficialTierPill />` and `<ProductLinePill />` lines with a single `<OfficialTierPicker />`.
- `i18n/locales/en.json` + `i18n/locales/zh.json` — add:
  - `filters.tierPicker.label` — "Official" (used in `Official: …` trigger formatter)
  - `filters.tierPicker.tierSection` — "Tier" / "级别"
  - `filters.tierPicker.lineSection` — "Product line" / "产品线"
  Keep the existing `filters.tier.*` (All / Unofficial / Product-Line / Company) and `filters.productLine.*` (All lines) keys — they're reused inside the popover. The standalone-rail-only keys (`filters.tierLabel`, `filters.productLineLabel`) can stay as aria-labels on the section groups or be removed if unreferenced — decide at edit time after grepping.
- `tests/e2e/approval.spec.ts` — three SSR specs hard-code button names:
  - line 18: `expect(html).toContain("Product-Line")` and `expect(html).toContain("Company")` — these run on the default tier=all listing, where the trigger now reads "Official: All" not the four tier names. Update assertions to look for the picker trigger label (e.g. `"Official:"`).
  - lines 48-54: `?tier=productLine` round-trip — replace `getByRole("button", { name: "Product-Line", exact: true })` + `aria-pressed` assertion with `getByRole("button", { name: /Official: Product-Line/ })`.
  - lines 66-79: `?tier=productLine&productLineId=wireless` — same, look for `Official: Wireless`. Drop the `getByRole("group", { name: "Product line" })` block (the pill rail group no longer exists at this layer) OR open the popover and assert the inner option's aria-pressed state.
  - the gated multi-actor flow (lines 110-119) calls `page.locator("#approvals-productLine").selectOption("wireless")` — that's the publish dialog, not the list rail; untouched.
- `app/components/approvals/ReviewerQueueTable.nuxt.test.ts` — unaffected (it's the admin queue, not the listing rail).

### Delete
- `app/components/filters/OfficialTierPill.vue` — replaced.
- `app/components/filters/ProductLinePill.vue` — replaced.
- Any test that mounts those two components directly. Quick grep before deletion.

### Leave alone
- `ScopePills.vue`, `DeptPicker.vue`, `PublisherPicker.vue`, `TagDrawer.vue` — unchanged.
- `ResultsSummary.vue` — the active-filter chips strip already builds chips from each filter key; quick check that it surfaces a Tier and Product Line chip when set (or add them if missing — separate small change).
- `shared/validators/filters.ts`, `shared/search/query.ts`, server endpoints — unchanged. URL contract is identical.

## Critical files

- `app/components/filters/FilterBar.vue` — the one-line swap
- `app/components/filters/OfficialTierPicker.vue` — the new component (model after `CreatorPicker.vue`)
- `tests/e2e/approval.spec.ts` — assertions that depend on the old pill buttons

## Verification

1. `bun run lint && bun run typecheck && bun run test` — should be green; expect e2e SSR specs to need touch-ups described above.
2. `bun dev`, visit `/en/extensions`:
   - Rail is one row; trigger reads `Official: All` (muted idle style).
   - Open the popover → two-row layout, Tier row shows 4 options, Product-Line row is hidden.
   - Click `Product-Line` → tier row shows it selected; product-line row appears below; trigger label updates to `Official: Product-Line`; popover stays open.
   - Click `Wireless` → trigger label updates to `Official: Wireless`; URL gains `?tier=productLine&productLineId=wireless`.
   - Click `Unofficial` → trigger reads `Official: Unofficial`, URL drops both `tier` and (critically) `productLineId` in one navigation.
   - Click outside → popover closes; trigger keeps the selected value.
3. Reload `/en/extensions?tier=productLine&productLineId=wireless` from a cold page → trigger renders as `Official: Wireless` server-side; opening the popover shows Wireless already selected.
4. `/zh/extensions` — same flow with `官方: 无线` / `级别` / `产品线` strings.
5. `playwright test tests/e2e/approval.spec.ts` — passes after the assertion updates.
6. Cross-check the active-filter chip strip below the rail surfaces a dismissible chip for the picked tier and product line; dismissing the chip clears the matching filter (and, for tier, also clears productLineId). If chips are missing today, add them in `ResultsSummary.vue` as a follow-up minor commit.

## Commit plan

Stays on the existing `feat/approvals-product-line-dimension` branch so the changes ride **PR #43** — no new PR. Two commits, then stop before push so the user can review.

1. `refactor(p9-ui-listing): collapse Tier and Product Line into a single Official picker` — adds `OfficialTierPicker.vue`, updates `FilterBar.vue`, adds i18n strings, removes the two old pill components, updates e2e assertions.
2. `docs(p9-ui-listing): note the picker collapse in features + ADR cross-reference` — short bilingual line in `docs/features.md` and `docs/daily-log.md`; one-line "2026-06-08 (followup)" note in ADR-0001 if anything in the addendum named the inline pill rail by component (a quick grep should be empty — the addendum only names the `ProductLinePill` file, which I'll update or remove the reference for).

Do **not** run `git push` after the commits — wait for the user to inspect the diff and give the green light.

b.sortOrder),\n)\nfunction lineLabel(line: ProductLine): string {\n  return locale.value === \"zh\" ? line.labelZh : line.labelEn\n}\nfunction lineLabelById(id: string | undefined): string | null {\n  if (!id) return null\n  const line = productLines.value.find((l) => l.id === id)\n  return line ? lineLabel(line) : id\n}\n\nconst activeTier = computed<Tier | undefined>(() => filters.value.tier)\nconst activeLineId = computed<string | undefined>(\n  () => filters.value.productLineId,\n)\nconst hasNarrow = computed(() => !!activeTier.value)\n\n// Trigger label — \"Official: {value}\".\n//\n// - undefined tier        → \"Official: All\"\n// - unofficial / company  → \"Official: <tier label>\"\n// - productLine, no line  → \"Official: Product-Line\"\n// - productLine + line    → \"Official: <line label>\" (more specific reads)\nconst triggerLabel = computed(() => {\n  const prefix = t(\"filters.tierPicker.triggerLabel\")\n  if (!activeTier.value) return `${prefix}: ${t(\"filters.tier.all\")}`\n  if (activeTier.value === \"productLine\") {\n    const line = lineLabelById(activeLineId.value)\n    if (line) return `${prefix}: ${line}`\n    return `${prefix}: ${t(\"filters.tier.productLine\")}`\n  }\n  return `${prefix}: ${t(`filters.tier.${activeTier.value}`)}`\n})\n\nfunction selectTier(tier: Tier | undefined) {\n  // Atomic update: switching away from productLine clears productLineId in\n  // the same navigation so the URL never carries a stale line on a tier\n  // that doesn't accept one (mirrors the iff-rule on the server side).\n  update({\n    tier,\n    productLineId: tier === \"productLine\" ? filters.value.productLineId : undefined,\n  })\n}\n\nfunction selectLine(productLineId: string | undefined) {\n  update({ productLineId })\n}\n</script>\n\n<template>\n  <Popover v-model:open=\"open\">\n    <PopoverTrigger\n      :class=\"[\n        'inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 rounded-md border px-2.5 py-0.5 text-[12px] transition-colors',\n        hasNarrow\n          ? 'border-(--color-ink)/20 bg-(--color-card) text-(--color-ink) font-semibold'\n          : 'border-(--color-border) bg-(--color-card) text-(--color-ink-muted) hover:text-(--color-ink)',\n      ]\"\n    >\n      <span class=\"truncate max-w-[140px]\">{{ triggerLabel }}</span>\n      <ChevronDown :size=\"12\" aria-hidden=\"true\" />\n    </PopoverTrigger>\n\n    <PopoverContent align=\"start\" :class=\"'w-[320px] p-3 space-y-3'\">\n      <!-- Tier row -->\n      <div>\n        <p class=\"mb-1.5 text-[11px] font-medium uppercase tracking-wide text-(--color-ink-muted)\">\n          {{ t(\"filters.tierLabel\") }}\n        </p>\n        <div\n          role=\"group\"\n          :aria-label=\"t('filters.tierLabel')\"\n          class=\"flex flex-wrap gap-1\"\n        >\n          <button\n            type=\"button\"\n            :aria-pressed=\"!activeTier\"\n            class=\"rounded-full border px-2.5 py-0.5 text-[12px] font-semibold transition\"\n            :class=\"\n              !activeTier\n                ? 'bg-(--color-ink)/8 text-(--color-ink) border-(--color-ink)/25'\n                : 'border-(--color-border) text-(--color-ink-muted) hover:text-(--color-ink)'\n            \"\n            @click=\"selectTier(undefined)\"\n          >\n            {{ t(\"filters.tier.all\") }}\n          </button>\n          <button\n            v-for=\"key in TIER_KEYS\"\n            :key=\"key\"\n            type=\"button\"\n            :aria-pressed=\"activeTier === key\"\n            class=\"rounded-full border px-2.5 py-0.5 text-[12px] font-semibold transition\"\n            :class=\"\n              activeTier === key\n                ? 'bg-(--color-ink)/8 text-(--color-ink) border-(--color-ink)/25'\n                : 'border-(--color-border) text-(--color-ink-muted) hover:text-(--color-ink)'\n            \"\n            @click=\"selectTier(key)\"\n          >\n            {{ t(`filters.tier.${key}`) }}\n          </button>\n        </div>\n      </div>\n\n      <!-- Product line row — only when productLine tier is active -->\n      <div v-if=\"activeTier === 'productLine'\">\n        <p class=\"mb-1.5 text-[11px] font-medium uppercase tracking-wide text-(--color-ink-muted)\">\n          {{ t(\"filters.productLineLabel\") }}\n        </p>\n        <div\n          role=\"group\"\n          :aria-label=\"t('filters.productLineLabel')\"\n          class=\"flex flex-wrap gap-1\"\n        >\n          <button\n            type=\"button\"\n            :aria-pressed=\"!activeLineId\"\n            class=\"rounded-full border px-2.5 py-0.5 text-[12px] font-semibold transition\"\n            :class=\"\n              !activeLineId\n                ? 'bg-(--color-ink)/8 text-(--color-ink) border-(--color-ink)/25'\n                : 'border-(--color-border) text-(--color-ink-muted) hover:text-(--color-ink)'\n            \"\n            @click=\"selectLine(undefined)\"\n          >\n            {{ t(\"filters.productLine.all\") }}\n          </button>\n          <button\n            v-for=\"line in orderedLines\"\n            :key=\"line.id\"\n            type=\"button\"\n            :aria-pressed=\"activeLineId === line.id\"\n            class=\"rounded-full border px-2.5 py-0.5 text-[12px] font-semibold transition\"\n            :class=\"\n              activeLineId === line.id\n                ? 'bg-(--color-ink)/8 text-(--color-ink) border-(--color-ink)/25'\n                : 'border-(--color-border) text-(--color-ink-muted) hover:text-(--color-ink)'\n            \"\n            @click=\"selectLine(line.id)\"\n          >\n            {{ lineLabel(line) }}\n          </button>\n        </div>\n      </div>\n    </PopoverContent>\n  </Popover>\n</template>\n"

15	### 2026-06-08
16	
17	**Briefing.** The official-tier approval workflow gains a product-line dimension. Product-Line Official is now per-line — Wireless / Datacom / Terminals / Cloud each get their own reviewer pool inside every functional category — and Company-tier admins of a given subCat can pick the Product-Line reviewers for that same subCat without a super-admin in the loop.
18	
19	<details>
20	<summary>Details</summary>
21	
22	- **Per-product-line endorsements** — Applying for Product-Line Official now requires picking a product line. The reviewer matrix at `/admin/reviewers` splits into two tabs: Company stays a single column per subCat, Product-Line becomes a 9 × 4 grid (subCats × product lines). Detail-page badges read "Wireless Official" / "无线官方" instead of the generic Product-Line label. (#43)
23	- **Delegated matrix edits** — Company-tier admins of subCat X can now manage the Product-Line reviewers for subCat X across every line, without escalating to a super-admin. Cells outside their subCat render greyed and read-only. Company-tier cells stay super-admin-only. (#43)
24	- **Product-line filter on the browse rail** — When the tier filter is set to Product-Line, a compact product-line pill rail appears next to it on the same row, honouring the single-row quiet pill style. `?tier=productLine&productLineId=wireless` round-trips through SSR. (#43)
25	- **`/api/v1` contract preserved** — Tier and product line are intentionally suppressed at the public-CLI boundary; `badge: "official"` still derives from `officialTier != null`. ADR-0001 picks up a dated addendum capturing the rationale for partial-unique indexes and the delegation rule. (#43)
26	
27	</details>

> DEVELOPER

now how to manage the extension for official or unofficial, is there a process?

> AGENT

Yes — there's a full end-to-end workflow, and a notable gap. Here's how it works today.

## Default state

Every newly-published extension is **Unofficial** (`extensions.officialTier IS NULL`). No application is needed to stay unofficial — that's just the default.

## Elevation: Unofficial → Official

**Publisher submits** (`app/components/approvals/RequestOfficialDialog.vue`)
1. Sign in as the extension's publisher.
2. Go to `/en/publish` (publisher dashboard).
3. Each published-but-unofficial extension row shows an **"Apply for official"** button.
4. The dialog asks for: target tier (Product-Line / Company), functional category (subCat), product line (only when tier=Product-Line), optional reason.
5. Submit → server inserts an `approval_requests` row with `status='pending'`. The extension row stays Unofficial during review.
6. The publisher's own row gains an **"Awaiting review"** pill.

**Reviewer decides** (`app/pages/admin/approvals/index.vue` → `ReviewerQueueTable.vue`)
1. Sign in as someone in the right cell of the matrix — `(tier, subCat, productLine?)`. Super-admins see every pending row.
2. Visit `/en/admin/approvals`.
3. Click **Approve** → in one transaction the server stamps `officialTier` (plus `productLineId` for Product-Line tier) on the extension and sets `approval_requests.status='approved'`. The badge appears on the card and detail-page hero.
4. Click **Reject** → opens an inline note, on confirm sets `status='rejected'`. The extension stays Unofficial; the publisher sees the note at `/profile?section=requests`.

**Publisher can withdraw** a still-pending request from `/profile?section=requests` → `status='withdrawn'`.

The state machine itself is pure code in `shared/approvals/state.ts` (`decideApprovalOutcome`, `decideWithdrawOutcome`); the orchestrator that runs it lives in `server/utils/approvals.ts`.

## Who can review what — matrix management

**Page**: `/en/admin/reviewers`. Tabbed into **Company** and **Product-Line**.

- **Super-admin** (membership role `superAdmin`, seeded via `SEED_SUPER_ADMIN_EMAIL`) — can edit any cell on either tab.
- **Company-tier admin of subCat X** — can add/remove Product-Line reviewers for **subCat X only**, across all four product lines. They can't touch Company-tier cells, can't touch other subCats. The matrix UI greys out cells they can't edit.

Per-cell authorisation lives in `server/utils/auth.ts:requireCellAdmin`.

## What's missing — Official → Unofficial (demotion)

There is **no UI today** to demote an Official extension back to Unofficial. ADR-0001 lists it as an open follow-up:

> **Tier revocation** — a super-admin removing a granted tier is not yet supported. Data model allows `null` already; needs a single orchestrator + endpoint.

The data model already accepts `null`, so the missing pieces are:
- An orchestrator function (e.g. `revokeTier`) that nulls `officialTier` + `productLineId` and emits an `extension/approval.revoked` event.
- A super-admin-gated endpoint and a button somewhere (probably on the detail page or `/admin/approvals` history view).
- An ADR-0001 update noting how revocation interacts with future re-application (re-apply, or banned?).

Other gaps from the ADR: notification fan-out (events fire but nothing emails) and an audit trail for matrix edits.

Want me to plan + implement the demotion flow? It's small — one new endpoint, one orchestrator function, a confirm dialog on the detail page or a button in the publisher dashboard, plus tests.

> AGENT

Yes — six creator users are seeded, with memberships wired up. But there's an important gap: **no passwords**, so you can't actually sign in via the UI as any of them yet.

## What `bun run db:seed` plants

**`scripts/seed.ts` (CREATORS, lines 33–39)** inserts six rows into `users`:

| email | name | role(s) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `amy@agentcenter.dev` | Amy Chen | super-admin + company reviewer for systemDesign / softDev / testing |
| `ben@agentcenter.dev` | Ben Park | publisher (owns demo extensions) + productLine reviewer for softDev / testing across all 4 lines |
| `cory@agentcenter.dev` | Cory Liu | publisher + productLine reviewer for network / embedded |
| `dao@agentcenter.dev` | Dao Tran | publisher + company reviewer for network / embedded / cloud + productLine reviewer for cloud |
| `eli@agentcenter.dev` | Eli Smith | publisher + productLine reviewer for docs / data |
| `fei@agentcenter.dev` | Fei Wang | publisher + company reviewer for docs / data / vcs + productLine reviewer for vcs |

Memberships:
- `superAdmin` — exactly one, controlled by `SEED_SUPER_ADMIN_EMAIL` (default `amy@agentcenter.dev`, see `DEFAULT_SUPER_ADMIN_EMAIL` in `shared/data/approval-reviewers.ts:40`).
- `publisher` — any creator who owns at least one demo extension.
- Reviewer assignments come from `shared/data/approval-reviewers.ts` (company tier + the productLine fan-out my earlier commit added — 9 subCats × 4 product lines = 36 productLine rows + 9 company rows).

Demo content also gets seeded: one pending Company-tier request (`calendar-agent` / data), one pending Product-Line / Wireless request (`mqtt-bridge` / network), one approved (`summarize` / docs), one rejected (`explain` / softDev). See `shared/data/approval-requests.ts`.

## The gap

The `accounts` table (Better Auth password storage) is **not** populated by the seed. The e2e file calls this out at `tests/e2e/approval.spec.ts:79-90`:

> The seed has been extended to set Better-Auth passwords on the `CREATORS` (e.g. via a `SEED_PASSWORD` env var). Today the seed only inserts the user row, so amy can't actually sign in via the sign-in page.

So right now, to actually sign in as `amy@agentcenter.dev` and click around the approval workflow, you'd need to either:
1. Sign up fresh through `/en/sign-up` and manually run SQL to graft a superAdmin membership onto your new user, or
2. Extend the seed to insert Better Auth `accounts` rows with a hashed password for each CREATOR (a one-off TS pass that unblocks the full e2e too).

## Approved Plan:
# Plan: Seed Better-Auth passwords for the demo CREATORS

## Context

`bun run db:seed` plants six demo users (`amy@agentcenter.dev`,
`ben`, `cory`, `dao`, `eli`, `fei`) into the `users` table along with
publisher / superAdmin / reviewer memberships — enough for the entire
approval workflow to render with realistic data. The seed does **not**
plant a Better-Auth `accounts` row for any of them, so none of those
identities can actually sign in via `/en/sign-in`. The Playwright
multi-actor flow already encodes that gap at
`tests/e2e/approval.spec.ts:79-90`:

> The seed has been extended to set Better-Auth passwords on the
> `CREATORS` (e.g. via a `SEED_PASSWORD` env var). Today the seed
> only inserts the user row, so amy can't actually sign in via the
> sign-in page.

This plan closes that gap so:

- You can click around the approval flow locally as amy / ben / dao /
  etc. without signing up a fresh account and grafting memberships.
- The gated `RUN_FULL_E2E` multi-actor test starts working out of the
  box (it already reads `SEED_PASSWORD` and defaults to
  `"agentcenter-dev-password"` on line 102).

## Approach

Better-Auth's own sign-up route writes the credential account row as:

```ts
linkAccount({
  userId: createdUser.id,
  providerId: "credential",
  accountId: createdUser.id,
  password: await ctx.context.password.hash(password),
})
```

(See `node_modules/better-auth/dist/api/routes/sign-up.mjs:233-238`.)

The hashing helper is `hashPassword` from `better-auth/crypto`, signature
`(password: string) => Promise<string>` — scrypt with embedded salt /
params, matched by Better-Auth's `verifyPassword` on sign-in.

The seed plants one credential account row per CREATOR using the same
shape and a deterministic id (`acc-credential-${userId}`) so re-running
the seed is idempotent. `onConflictDoUpdate` refreshes the stored hash
whenever `SEED_PASSWORD` changes, so rotating credentials is just
`SEED_PASSWORD=newvalue bun run db:seed`.

## Files to change

### `scripts/seed.ts`

Add — right after `await db.insert(users).values(CREATORS).onConflictDoNothing()` (currently line 165):

- Import `hashPassword` from `better-auth/crypto`.
- Import `accounts` from `~~/shared/db/schema`.
- Read `SEED_PASSWORD` from env, default to `"agentcenter-dev-password"`
  (matches the e2e default on `tests/e2e/approval.spec.ts:102` so both
  paths line up).
- Hash once (all six users share the same dev password).
- Build the rows:
  ```ts
  CREATORS.map((u) => ({
    id: `acc-credential-${u.id}`,
    userId: u.id,
    accountId: u.id,
    providerId: "credential",
    password: hash,
  }))
  ```
- Insert with `.onConflictDoUpdate({ target: accounts.id, set: { password: hash, updatedAt: new Date() } })` so password rotation actually rotates.
- One `console.log` line ("seed: planted credential accounts for N creators (password from SEED_PASSWORD or default)") that mirrors the surrounding seed log style.

### `tests/e2e/approval.spec.ts`

The skip guard at lines 79-96 currently reads:

```ts
test.beforeAll(() => {
  test.skip(
    !process.env.RUN_FULL_E2E,
    "Gated on RUN_FULL_E2E. Also requires seeded passwords on CREATORS — see comment above.",
  )
})
```

- Drop the "Also requires seeded passwords on CREATORS" half from the
  skip reason — that prerequisite is now satisfied by the seed.
- Drop the outdated 2-paragraph comment about the password gap above
  the describe block; replace with a one-liner pointing at the seeded
  default password.

### `CLAUDE.md`

Add one short bullet under `## Workflow` (or a new sub-bullet anywhere
the seed is mentioned) so future planning agents know the credentials:

> Dev sign-in: `bun run db:seed` plants six users on
> `*@agentcenter.dev` (amy = super-admin, the rest publishers /
> reviewers). Password comes from `SEED_PASSWORD`, default
> `"agentcenter-dev-password"`. Rotate by re-running the seed with a
> new env value.

### `docs/daily-log.md`

Short bilingual one-liner under a fresh `2026-06-08-c` entry (or appended
to the existing 2026-06-08 entries) noting that the demo accounts can
now sign in.

## Critical files

- `scripts/seed.ts` — the only file that actually changes behaviour
- `tests/e2e/approval.spec.ts` — paragraph cleanup
- `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/daily-log.md` — short notes

No new tests are needed: the seed-correctness check is "I can sign in
as amy / ben in the browser" and the gated e2e flow will run end-to-end
once `RUN_FULL_E2E=1` is set.

## Verification

1. `bun run db:migrate && bun run db:seed` — fresh DB.
2. Visit `http://localhost:3000/en/sign-in`, enter `amy@agentcenter.dev`
   / `agentcenter-dev-password`. Should redirect to the home page; the
   TopBar shows Amy's avatar / name.
3. As amy, navigate to `/en/admin/reviewers` — the matrix loads with
   every cell editable (amy is super-admin).
4. Sign out, sign in as `dao@agentcenter.dev` (same password). As a
   non-super company admin for `cloud`, `/en/admin/reviewers` should
   show productLine cells of `cloud` editable and others greyed out.
5. `SEED_PASSWORD=foobar bun run db:seed` — re-running should print
   "planted credential accounts" without errors; sign-in as amy now
   needs `foobar`, the old password fails.
6. `RUN_FULL_E2E=1 bun run test:e2e tests/e2e/approval.spec.ts` —
   the multi-actor golden path runs end-to-end (publisher submits,
   reviewer approves, badge appears).
7. `bun run validate` — green at 36 / 352 tests as before; the seed
   isn't executed by validate, so no test surface change is expected.

## Commit plan

Stays on `feat/approvals-product-line-dimension` so the change rides
**PR #43** — no new PR. One commit, then stop before push so the user
can review locally first.

Three follow-ups from ADR-0001 are still open, plus a couple of practical gaps that surfaced while shipping #43. In order of "most useful for the current product":

1. **Tier revocation (Official → Unofficial)** — biggest gap. Today there's no UI to demote an Official extension. A super-admin can manually `UPDATE extensions SET official_tier = NULL` but that's a footgun. Small change: one orchestrator function (`revokeTier`), one super-admin-gated endpoint, a confirm button on the detail page (admin only), tests. ~half day.

2. **Approvals queue filtering** — `/admin/approvals` shows every pending request the reviewer can decide. With the productLine dimension, a reviewer assigned to four `(cloud × wireless|datacom|terminals|cloud)` cells now sees four cells worth of requests in one undifferentiated list. Adding tier / subCat / productLine pill filters above the queue (reusing the picker pattern from the list page) makes triage faster. ~half day.

3. **Notification fan-out** — the orchestrator already emits `extension/approval.{requested,decided}` Inngest events, but the consumer just logs them. Wiring real notifications (email via Resend or in-app via a `notifications` table) means publishers know when their request lands without polling `/profile?section=requests`. ~1 day.

4. **Audit trail for matrix edits** — least urgent. Today super-admin matrix changes leave no record. A `audit_events` table + a write call on each assign/unassign + a small admin viewer. ~half day.

5. **Filter-rail micro-fixes** — minor: the active-filter chip strip in `ResultsSummary.vue` probably doesn't surface `tier` or `productLineId` as chips today (the rail picker swap shouldn't affect that, but it deserves a quick check). 30 min.

If you want one to plan now, I'd pick **#1 (tier revocation)** — it closes the loudest gap in the workflow we just shipped, has the clearest UX scope, and doesn't depend on infra (Inngest consumers, Resend, etc.) the project doesn't yet have. Want me to plan that, or pick a different one?

## Tier Revocation Feature — Existing Surface Mapping

I've completed a read-only audit of the approval workflow surfaces. Here's what's there:

---

### 1. **Pure State Machine** (`shared/approvals/state.ts`, lines 1–92)

The state machine is intentionally minimal. Key types:

```typescript
export type OfficialTier = "productLine" | "company"
export type ApprovalStatus = "pending" | "approved" | "rejected" | "withdrawn"
export type ApprovalAction =
  | { decision: "approve" }
  | { decision: "reject"; note?: string }
```

Return types from decision functions:

```typescript
export interface ApprovalOutcome {
  request: ApprovalRequestPatch  // status, decidedByUserId, decidedAt, reviewerNote
  extension?: ExtensionOfficialTierPatch  // { officialTier }
}
```

**Verdict on revocation placement**: The current state machine models *approval workflows* (request-driven transitions). Revocation is a **separate, out-of-band operation** initiated by super-admin decree, not via `approval_requests`. It should NOT live in the state machine; instead, it needs its own orchestrator function (`revokeTier`) in `server/utils/approvals.ts` that directly calls the repository's tier-setter without going through `decideApprovalOutcome`.

---

### 2. **Orchestrator** (`server/utils/approvals.ts`, lines 1–264)

Three main functions with their signatures and patterns:

```typescript
// SubmitParams: extensionId, requestedTier, subCat, productLineId, userId, reason
async function submitRequest(params: SubmitParams): Promise<ApprovalRequestRow>
  // Emits: { name: "extension/approval.requested", data: { requestId, extensionId, requestedTier, subCat, productLineId, requesterUserId } }

// DecideParams: requestId, action, reviewerUserId
async function decideRequest(params: DecideParams): Promise<ApprovalRequestRow>
  // Calls: approvalsRepo.applyDecision(tx, requestId, outcome.request)
  // Calls: approvalsRepo.setExtensionOfficialTier(tx, extensionId, tier, productLineId) [only if approved]
  // Emits: { name: "extension/approval.decided", data: { requestId, extensionId, decision, decidedByUserId } }

// WithdrawParams: requestId, userId
async function withdrawRequest(params: WithdrawParams): Promise<ApprovalRequestRow>
  // Calls: approvalsRepo.applyWithdraw(db, requestId, decidedAt)
  // [Note: no Inngest event currently fired]
```

**ApprovalErrorCode enum** (lines 19–30): `extension_not_found | not_publisher_owner | extension_not_published | request_not_found | request_not_pending | duplicate_pending_request | not_reviewer | not_requester | missing_product_line | unexpected_product_line`

**Pattern for new `revokeTier` function**:
- Params: `{ extensionId: string; revocationNote?: string; superAdminUserId: string }`
- Return: `ApprovalRequestRow` (for audit trail, though revocation doesn't create an actual request row)
- Should add error codes: `extension_not_found`, `extension_not_official` (tier is already null), possibly `not_super_admin` (though that's gated at endpoint level)
- Calls `approvalsRepo.setExtensionOfficialTier(tx, extensionId, null, null)` to clear both fields
- Emits: `{ name: "extension/tier.revoked", data: { extensionId, revokedByUserId, revokedAt, note? } }`

**Super-admin gate pattern** (from `by-email.get.ts`):
