```

**Cell-admin gate pattern** (from `assign.post.ts`, lines 8–16):

**Error mapping pattern** (from `submit.post.ts`):
```typescript
const ERROR_STATUS: Record<string, number> = {
  extension_not_found: 404,
  not_publisher_owner: 403,
  extension_not_published: 409,
  duplicate_pending_request: 409,
  missing_product_line: 400,
  unexpected_product_line: 400,
}

try {
  const row = await submitRequest(params)
  return { ok: true, request: row }
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof ApprovalError) {
    const status = ERROR_STATUS[err.code] ?? 400
    throw createError({ statusCode: status, statusMessage: err.code })
  }
}
```

**New endpoint convention**: Place at `/api/internal/approvals/revoke.post.ts` (super-admin only). Error mapping should include `extension_not_official: 409` (already null).

## Approved Plan:
# Plan: Tier revocation (Official → Unofficial)

## Context

ADR-0001 calls out tier revocation as the most load-bearing open
follow-up: a super-admin removing a granted tier is not yet supported.
The data model already allows `extensions.officialTier IS NULL`, but
the only existing path to it is "never approved." If a Company Official
extension turns out to be broken / policy-violating / approved by
mistake, the only fix today is hand-rolled SQL.

This plan adds a one-step revocation: a super-admin opens an Official
extension's detail page, clicks **Revoke**, writes a required reason
note (mirroring the existing reject flow), and the badge disappears.
The publisher sees the revocation reason on their dashboard so they
know what happened. They can apply for elevation again immediately;
the revocation metadata clears on the next approval.

User decisions captured upstream:
1. **Note required**, same bar as Reject (`approvals.errors` already
   surfaces the note to the publisher).
2. **Revoke button lives on the detail page hero**, gated on
   `isSuperAdmin`. No new admin list page in this scope.
3. **Pending elevation requests are left alone**. Revocation clears the
   *current* tier; a pending request asks for a *future* tier. They're
   independent.

## Data model — migration 0011

Add three nullable columns to `extensions` for the revocation audit
trail. Keeping them on the row itself (not a separate table) is the
"single source of truth" choice: when the publisher's dashboard renders
"why am I no longer Official?", the answer is one JOIN-free read.

| column | type | notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `revoked_at` | `timestamptz` nullable | the timestamp |
| `revoked_by_user_id` | `text` nullable, `references users.id ON DELETE SET NULL` | so deleting an admin doesn't fail revocation history; just orphans the attribution |
| `revocation_note` | `text` nullable | bounded at the validator |

No CHECK constraint coupling — these fields are independent of
`officialTier`. The orchestrator owns the invariant: when tier becomes
non-null (re-elevation), all three revocation fields clear; when tier
goes to null via revocation, all three populate.

## Repository layer

`server/repositories/approvals.ts`:

- **Extend `setExtensionOfficialTier(db, extensionId, tier, productLineId)`** — when `tier` is non-null, ALSO set `revokedAt=null, revokedByUserId=null, revocationNote=null` in the same UPDATE. Cleanest place to enforce the re-elevation-clears-revocation rule.
- **New `applyRevocation(db, params)`** — single UPDATE that sets `officialTier=null, productLineId=null, revokedAt=now, revokedByUserId, revocationNote` atomically. Returns the affected row count for the orchestrator's "was it actually Official?" guard.

`server/repositories/extensions.ts` — extend `detailSelect` and the publisher-dashboard select to include the three new columns so the UI can read them in one round-trip.

## Orchestrator

`server/utils/approvals.ts`:

```ts
export interface RevokeTierParams {
  extensionId: string
  superAdminUserId: string
  note: string
}

export async function revokeTier(params: RevokeTierParams)
  : Promise<{ extensionId: string; revokedAt: Date }>
```

- Loads extension via `extensionsRepo.findById`. Missing → `extension_not_found`.
- If `officialTier IS NULL` → throw new error code `extension_not_official` (409). Idempotent guard.
- `db.transaction` → `applyRevocation(...)`. If affected rows === 0 (race lost), throw `extension_not_official`.
- Emit Inngest event `extension/tier.revoked` with `{ extensionId, revokedByUserId, revokedAt, note }`. The existing `notify-approval` consumer picks it up by event name (new handler block — small) and emails the publisher.

Add to `ApprovalErrorCode`: `extension_not_official`. The super-admin role check happens at the endpoint layer (`requireSuperAdmin`), not the orchestrator, mirroring the existing pattern for assign/unassign.

## Validator

`shared/validators/approvals.ts`:

```ts
export const REVOKE_NOTE_MAX = 500  // matches APPROVAL_NOTE_MAX

export const RevokeTierSchema = z.object({
  extensionId: z.string().trim().min(1),
  note: z.string().trim().min(1).max(REVOKE_NOTE_MAX),
})
```

The `.min(1)` after `.trim()` enforces "required, not whitespace-only".

## Endpoint

`server/api/internal/approvals/revoke.post.ts` — new. Pattern: copy
`submit.post.ts` (validator → try/catch → status mapping). Gate on
`await requireSuperAdmin(event)` from `server/utils/auth.ts`.

Error status table:
```ts
extension_not_found: 404,
extension_not_official: 409,
```

## Admin role surfacing for the detail page

`server/api/internal/admin/me.get.ts` already returns
`{ isSuperAdmin, isReviewer }`. The detail page doesn't call it today.
Add a `useFetch("/api/internal/admin/me", { default: ... })` call from
the detail page so it can flow `viewer.isSuperAdmin` into ExtHero. The
endpoint returns `isSuperAdmin: false` (or the loader's default) for
anonymous callers, so the button stays hidden by default.

## UI

**`app/components/extension/ExtHero.vue`**:
- New prop `canRevoke: boolean`.
- Render a small "Revoke" button (`text-[11px]`, outline style — quieter than the existing primary Install) only when `canRevoke && officialTier`. Sits next to the badge so it's spatially anchored to the thing it operates on.
- Click → emits `revoke` event; the page hosts the dialog.

**`app/components/approvals/RevokeTierDialog.vue`** — new. Model
after `RequestOfficialDialog.vue`:
- `<Dialog v-model:open>` shell.
- Title + subtitle that names the extension.
- Single required `<Textarea>` for the note (bound to `note`, maxlength
  500, counter).
- Cancel + Confirm buttons; Confirm disabled while note is empty or busy.
- POST `/api/internal/approvals/revoke` with `{ extensionId, note }`.
- On 200: emit `revoked`, close. The detail page refreshes its
  `useFetch` data so the badge disappears + the button hides itself
  (no more `officialTier`).
- On error: surface the localized message via `te()` lookup against
  `approvals.errors.<code>` with the generic fallback (same pattern as
  RequestOfficialDialog).

**`app/pages/extensions/[slug].vue`** — host the dialog, plumb the
`canRevoke` prop into ExtHero, refresh on `revoked` event.

**Publisher dashboard surfacing** — when a row has `revokedAt != null`
and `officialTier === null`, render one extra muted line under the
title: "Revoked on {date} by {admin}. Reason: {note}" (i18n key
`approvals.revokedAnnotation`). When the publisher applies again and
gets approved, the orchestrator clears these fields → annotation
disappears automatically. Need a one-liner change in the dashboard
loader's select to include the revocation columns and admin name.

## i18n keys (en + zh)

- `approvals.revoke.button` — "Revoke" / "撤销"
- `approvals.revoke.title` — "Revoke Official status" / "撤销官方认证"
- `approvals.revoke.subtitle` — "Demote \"{name}\" back to Unofficial. The publisher will see your reason." / "将「{name}」降级为非官方，发布者会看到你填写的理由。"
- `approvals.revoke.noteLabel` — "Reason (required)" / "理由（必填）"
- `approvals.revoke.notePlaceholder` — "What's the reason for revocation?" / "为何撤销？"
- `approvals.revoke.cancel` / `approvals.revoke.confirm` — "Cancel" / "Confirm revoke" / "取消" / "确认撤销"
- `approvals.revokedAnnotation` — "Revoked on {date} by {admin}: {note}" / "于 {date} 被 {admin} 撤销：{note}"
- `approvals.errors.extension_not_official` — "This extension isn't Official, nothing to revoke." / "该扩展并非官方扩展，无需撤销。"

## Tests

- `server/utils/approvals.test.ts` — three new tests under a `describe("revokeTier")` block:
  - happy path: super-admin revokes a `company`-tier extension; `applyRevocation` called with correct args; event fires with `extension/tier.revoked`.
  - `extension_not_found` short-circuit when `findById` returns null.
  - `extension_not_official` short-circuit when the row's `officialTier` is null.
- `tests/integration/repositories/approvals.test.ts` — new test: `setExtensionOfficialTier` re-stamping to a non-null tier clears `revokedAt`, `revokedByUserId`, `revocationNote` on the same row.
- `tests/e2e/approval.spec.ts` — SSR check that anonymous load of an Official detail page does NOT contain the localized "Revoke" button text. (The role-gated positive case rides on the existing gated multi-actor block.)
- Component test for `RevokeTierDialog.vue` — submit-disabled-on-empty-note, fetch payload shape, error mapping.

222	// matching `productLineId` (null for company tier) on the parent extension.
223	// Lives here (rather than in `extensions.ts`) because the approval
224	// orchestrator is the only legitimate writer; keeping the call adjacent to
225	// the request mutation makes that intent obvious. The DB CHECK enforces
226	// productLineId is non-null iff tier='productLine', so a bad pair from a
227	// caller is rejected at the boundary.
228	export async function setExtensionOfficialTier(
229	  db: Transactable,
230	  extensionId: string,
231	  tier: OfficialTier,
232	  productLineId: string | null,
233	): Promise<void> {

The DB CHECK enforces\n// productLineId is non-null iff tier='productLine', so a bad pair from a\n// caller is rejected at the boundary.\nexport async function setExtensionOfficialTier(\n  db: Transactable,\n  extensionId: string,\n  tier: OfficialTier,\n  productLineId: string | null,\n): Promise<void> {\n  await db\n    .update(extensions)\n    .set({ officialTier: tier, productLineId, updatedAt: new Date() })\n    .where(eq(extensions.id, extensionId))\n}",
  "new_string": "// Companion mutator for the approve path — stamps `officialTier` and the\n// matching `productLineId` (null for company tier) on the parent extension.\n// Lives here (rather than in `extensions.ts`) because the approval\n// orchestrator is the only legitimate writer; keeping the call adjacent to\n// the request mutation makes that intent obvious. The DB CHECK enforces\n// productLineId is non-null iff tier='productLine', so a bad pair from a\n// caller is rejected at the boundary. Also clears the revocation audit\n// fields in the same UPDATE — the invariant is \"you're either currently\n// Official with no pending revocation explanation, or Unofficial\".\nexport async function setExtensionOfficialTier(\n  db: Transactable,\n  extensionId: string,\n  tier: OfficialTier,\n  productLineId: string | null,\n): Promise<void> {\n  await db\n    .update(extensions)\n    .set({\n      officialTier: tier,\n      productLineId,\n      revokedAt: null,\n      revokedByUserId: null,\n      revocationNote: null,\n      updatedAt: new Date(),\n    })\n    .where(eq(extensions.id, extensionId))\n}\n\n// Companion mutator for the revoke path — atomically clears\n// `officialTier` and `productLineId` while writing the audit trio\n// (`revokedAt`, `revokedByUserId`, `revocationNote`). The orchestrator's\n// pre-check already confirmed the row was Official; this method's\n// returned affected-row count is the race-safe equivalent of a CAS,\n// surfacing \"someone else already revoked / re-approved\" as a 0.\nexport interface RevocationPatch {\n  revokedAt: Date\n  revokedByUserId: string\n  revocationNote: string\n}\nexport async function applyRevocation(\n  db: Transactable,\n  extensionId: string,\n  patch: RevocationPatch,\n): Promise<number> {\n  const updated = await db\n    .update(extensions)\n    .set({\n      officialTier: null,\n      productLineId: null,\n      revokedAt: patch.revokedAt,\n      revokedByUserId: patch.revokedByUserId,\n      revocationNote: patch.revocationNote,\n      updatedAt: new Date(),\n    })\n    .where(\n      and(\n        eq(extensions.id, extensionId),\n        sql`${extensions.officialTier} IS NOT NULL`,\n      ),\n    )\n    .returning({ id: extensions.id })\n  return updated.length\n}"
}

  "content": "import {\n  ApprovalError,\n  revokeTier,\n} from \"~~/server/utils/approvals\"\nimport { RevokeTierSchema } from \"~~/shared/validators/approvals\"\n\n// Super-admin Revoke action from the extension detail page. The role\n// gate sits here (requireSuperAdmin) so the orchestrator stays a pure\n// state-transition function — same pattern as the assign/unassign\n// endpoints. The validator's .trim().min(1) on the note caches a\n// whitespace-only submission before we touch the DB.\nconst ERROR_STATUS: Record<string, number> = {\n  extension_not_found: 404,\n  extension_not_official: 409,\n}\n\nexport default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {\n  const user = await requireSuperAdmin(event)\n  const body = await readValidatedBody(event, (raw) =>\n    RevokeTierSchema.parse(raw),\n  )\n\n  try {\n    const result = await revokeTier({\n      extensionId: body.extensionId,\n      superAdminUserId: user.id,\n      note: body.note,\n    })\n    return { ok: true, revocation: result }\n  } catch (err) {\n    if (err instanceof ApprovalError) {\n      const status = ERROR_STATUS[err.code] ?? 400\n      throw createError({ statusCode: status, statusMessage: err.code })\n    }\n    console.error(\"internal revokeTier failed\", err)\n    throw createError({\n      statusCode: 500,\n      statusMessage: \"approval_revoke_failed\",\n    })\n  }\n})\n"
}

1	// Gate the /admin/approvals page. Requires the caller to either hold a
2	// `superAdmin` membership or be assigned to at least one (tier, subCat)
3	// cell in the reviewer matrix. Authentication is enforced separately via
4	// `require-auth` — apply this middleware after it.
5	export default defineNuxtRouteMiddleware(async () => {
6	  const localePath = useLocalePath()
7	  try {
8	    const headers = import.meta.server
9	      ? useRequestHeaders(["cookie"])
10	      : {}
11	    const me = await $fetch("/api/internal/admin/me", {
12	      headers: headers as Record<string, string>,
13	    })
14	    if (!me.isReviewer) {
15	      return navigateTo(localePath("/"))
16	    }
17	  } catch {
18	    return navigateTo(localePath("/sign-in"))
19	  }
20	})

String((err as { statusMessage: unknown }).statusMessage)\n        : null\n    const key = status ? `approvals.errors.${status}` : null\n    error.value = key && te(key) ? t(key) : t(\"approvals.errors.generic\")\n  } finally {\n    busy.value = false\n  }\n}\n</script>\n\n<template>\n  <Dialog :open=\"open\" @update:open=\"(v) => emit('update:open', v)\">\n    <DialogContent <div>\n          <Label for=\"revoke-note\" class=\"text-xs font-medium\">\n            {{ t(\"approvals.revoke.noteLabel\") }}\n          </Label>\n          <Textarea\n class=\"mt-1 w-full\"\n          />\n          <p class=\"mt-1 text-right text-xs text-(--color-ink-muted)\">\n            {{ note.length }} / {{ REVOKE_NOTE_MAX }}\n          </p>\n        </div>\n\n        <p v-if=\"error\" class=\"text-sm text-red-600\">{{ error }}</p>\n\n        <div class=\"flex items-center justify-end gap-2\">\n          <DialogClose as-child>\n            <button\n              type=\"button\"\n              class=\"rounded-md px-3 py-1.5 text-sm text-(--color-ink-muted) hover:text-(--color-ink)\"\n            >\n              {{ t(\"approvals.revoke.cancel\") }}\n            </button>\n          </DialogClose>\n          <button\n            type=\"submit\"\n            :disabled=\"!canSubmit\"\n            class=\"inline-flex items-center gap-2 rounded-md bg-red-600   "new_string": "export async function getMyExtensions(userId: string) {\n  const db = useDb()\n  // Aliased join against `users` so we can pull the display name for whoever\n  // revoked the extension (if anyone) without colliding with the publisher's\n  // own user row downstream.\n  const revoker = alias(users, \"revoker\")\n  const rows = await db\n    .select({\n      id: extensions.id,\n      slug: extensions.slug,\n      name: extensions.name,\n      category: extensions.category,\n      visibility: extensions.visibility,\n      subCat: extensions.subCat,\n      officialTier: extensions.officialTier,\n      revokedAt: extensions.revokedAt,\n      revokedByUserId: extensions.revokedByUserId,\n      revocationNote: extensions.revocationNote,\n      revokedByName: revoker.name,\n      revokedByEmail: revoker.email,\n      createdAt: extensions.createdAt,\n      latestVersionId: extensionVersions.id,\n      latestVersion: extensionVersions.version,\n      latestStatus: extensionVersions.status,\n      latestBundleFileId: extensionVersions.bundleFileId,\n    })\n    .from(extensions)\n    .leftJoin(\n      extensionVersions,\n      eq(extensionVersions.extensionId, extensions.id),\n    )\n    .leftJoin(revoker, eq(revoker.id, extensions.revokedByUserId))\n    .where(eq(extensions.publisherUserId, userId))\n    .orderBy(desc(extensions.createdAt), desc(extensionVersions.createdAt))"
}

Data model allows `null` already; needs a single\norchestrator + endpoint.\" We've now closed it.\n\nDesign:\n\n- **Trigger lives on the detail page**, next to the badge, gated on\n  `admin/me.isSuperAdmin && officialTier`. Super-admins find an\n  extension the same way as anyone else — by browsing — and act\n  spatially next to the thing they're operating on. We deliberately\n  did not add a dedicated `/admin/officials` list page for v1; if bulk\n  audits become a need, that's an additive page later.\n- **Reason note is required**, matching the existing Reject flow.\n  `RevokeTierSchema` enforces `.trim().min(1)`; the publisher sees the\n  reason verbatim on their dashboard so a missing note would leave\n  them in the dark.\n- **Pending elevation requests are left alone.** Revocation clears the\n  *current* tier; a pending request asks for a *future* tier. Coupling\n  them would mean a Company-Official extension with a pending\n  Wireless productLine request can't be revoked without also\n  withdrawing the unrelated request — confusing for everyone.\n\nAudit trail strategy:\n\n- **Three new columns on `extensions`**: `revoked_at`,\n  `revoked_by_user_id` (FK to `users` with `ON DELETE SET NULL`),\n  `revocation_note`. Kept on the row itself rather than in a separate\n  `audit_events` table because the publisher dashboard's \"why am I no\n  longer Official?\" answer is one JOIN-free read.\n- **`setExtensionOfficialTier` extends to clear the trio** in the same\n  UPDATE whenever a tier is stamped. The invariant \"you're either\n  currently Official with no pending revocation explanation, or\n  Unofficial\" lives in the repo, not scattered across orchestrator\n  branches.\n- **`applyRevocation` is a CAS** via `WHERE official_tier IS NOT NULL`:\n  the returned affected-row count tells the orchestrator whether the\n  row actually transitioned, so a concurrent revoke / re-approve\n  surfaces cleanly as `extension_not_official` rather than silently\n  no-op'ing.\n\nInngest event `extension/tier.revoked` fires with `{ extensionId,\nrevokedByUserId, revokedAt, note }`. The existing notify-approval\nconsumer hasn't been wired to it yet — that's the next follow-up.\n\nWhat we gave up:\n\n- A dedicated `audit_events` table would survive across the\n  Official→Unofficial→Official cycle. Today the columns clear on\n  re-approval, so once an extension is back to Official the prior\n  revocation history is gone. That's intentional: the columns answer\n  \"what's happening now?\", not \"what's ever happened?\" If you need\n  durable history, the table is a separate ADR.\n\nCross-references for this update:\n\n- Migration: `drizzle/0011_warm_mandrill.sql`\n- Schema: `shared/db/schema/extension.ts` (revokedAt / revokedByUserId / revocationNote columns)\n- Repo: `server/repositories/approvals.ts` (`applyRevocation`,\n  extended `setExtensionOfficialTier`)\n- Orchestrator: `server/utils/approvals.ts` (`revokeTier`,\n  `extension_not_official` code)\n- Endpoint: `server/api/internal/approvals/revoke.post.ts`\n- UI: `app/components/extension/ExtHero.vue` (canRevoke prop +\n  button), `app/components/approvals/RevokeTierDialog.vue`,\n  `app/pages/extensions/[slug].vue` (admin/me fetch + dialog host),\n  `app/pages/publish/index.vue` (revocation annotation row)\nEOF",

39:12. **Official-tier approval workflow**: extensions default to Unofficial; elevation to Product-Line Official or Company Official goes through a reviewer matrix indexed by `(tier × FUNC_TAXONOMY subCat)`, additionally keyed by `productLine` (data-driven `product_lines` table; current rows: wireless, datacom, terminals, cloud) for the `productLine` tier only. Tiers are independent (no PL→Company ladder), `officialTier` lives in its own enum column, and the `/api/v1` `badge` field is read-derived from it to preserve the frozen CLI contract. Matrix edits: super-admins everywhere; company-tier admins of a given subCat may manage productLine-tier admins for the same subCat. Full rationale and trade-offs in `docs/adr/0001-official-tier-approval-workflow.md` (including the 2026-06-08 update).

### 3. Orchestrator: `listReviewerQueue`

**File: `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/server/utils/approvals.ts`** (lines 275–309)

Signature and body:
```typescript
export async function listReviewerQueue(
  userId: string,
): Promise<approvalsRepo.ApprovalRequestRow[]> {
  const db = useDb()
  if (await reviewersRepo.isSuperAdmin(db, userId)) {
    // Treat super-admin as "assigned to every cell". Pulled from the matrix
    // verbatim so an empty matrix still surfaces no rows — better than a
    // silent firehose. Productline IS NULL is encoded as the literal '∅' in
    // the dedup key so a (company, cloud, null) cell doesn't collapse onto
    // (productLine, cloud, '') by accident.
    const cells = await reviewersRepo
      .listMatrix(db)
      .then((rows) =>
        Array.from(
          new Set(
            rows.map((r) => `${r.tier}:${r.subCat}:${r.productLineId ?? "∅"}`),
          ),
        ).map((k) => {
          const [tier, subCat, pl] = k.split(":") as [OfficialTier, string, string]
          return {
            tier,
            subCat,
            productLineId: pl === "∅" ? null : pl,
          }
        }),
      )
    return approvalsRepo.listPendingForCells(db, cells)
  }

  const cells = await reviewersRepo.listCellsForUser(db, userId)
  return approvalsRepo.listPendingForCells(db, cells)
}
```

To add `filters?: { tier?, subCat?, productLineId? }`, the function would accept that parameter and pass it to `listPendingForCells`, which already receives a `cells` array. The filter intersection would narrow the cells before the DB query.

### 4. `listPendingForCells` Repository

**File: `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/server/repositories/approvals.ts`** (lines 138–169)

Function signature and body:
```typescript
export async function listPendingForCells(
  db: Transactable,
  cells: Array<{ tier: OfficialTier; subCat: string; productLineId: string | null }>,
): Promise<ApprovalRequestRow[]> {
  if (cells.length === 0) return []
  const cellMatches = cells.map((c) =>
    and(
      eq(approvalRequests.requestedTier, c.tier),
      eq(approvalRequests.subCat, c.subCat),
      c.productLineId === null
        ? isNull(approvalRequests.productLineId)
        : eq(approvalRequests.productLineId, c.productLineId),
    ),
  )
  return db
    .select(fullSelect)
    .from(approvalRequests)
    .where(
      and(
        eq(approvalRequests.status, "pending"),
        sql`(${sql.join(cellMatches, sql` OR `)})`,
      ),
    )
    .orderBy(desc(approvalRequests.createdAt))
}
```

The cell array takes objects with shape `{ tier: OfficialTier; subCat: string; productLineId: string | null }`. Filter intersection would pre-filter this array before passing to `listPendingForCells`.

### 5. Picker Pattern: `OfficialTierPicker.vue`

**File: `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/app/components/filters/OfficialTierPicker.vue`** (lines 1–107)

const { t, locale } = useI18n()
const { filters, update } = useFilters()

const activeTier = computed<Tier | undefined>(() => filters.value.tier)
const activeLineId = computed<string | undefined>(
  () => filters.value.productLineId,
)
const hasNarrow = computed(() => !!activeTier.value)

const triggerLabel = computed(() => {
  const prefix = t("filters.tierPicker.triggerLabel")
  if (!activeTier.value) return `${prefix}: ${t("filters.tier.all")}`
  if (activeTier.value === "productLine") {
    const line = lineLabelById(activeLineId.value)
    if (line) return `${prefix}: ${line}`
    return `${prefix}: ${t("filters.tier.productLine")}`
  }
  return `${prefix}: ${t(`filters.tier.${activeTier.value}`)}`
})

function selectTier(tier: Tier | undefined) {
  update({
    tier,
    productLineId: tier === "productLine" ? filters.value.productLineId : undefined,
  })
}

function selectLine(productLineId: string | undefined) {
  update({ productLineId })
}
```

**useFilters composable:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/app/composables/useFilters.ts` (lines 1–46)

URL state management:
```typescript
export function useFilters() {
  const route = useRoute()
  const router = useRouter()
  const localePath = useLocalePath()

  const filters = computed<Filters>(() => {
    const params = new URLSearchParams()
    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(route.query)) {
      if (Array.isArray(v)) {
        for (const item of v) if (item !== null) params.append(k, String(item))
      } else if (v !== null && v !== undefined) {
        params.append(k, String(v))
      }
    }
    return parseFilters(searchParamsToInput(params))
  })

  function update(partial: FilterUpdate) {
    const next: FilterUpdate = { ...filters.value, ...partial }
    if (!("page" in partial)) next.page = undefined
    const params = serializeFilters(next)
    const qs = params.toString()
    const path = route.path
    router.replace(qs ? `${path}?${qs}` : path)
  }

  function hrefForFilters(partial: FilterUpdate, basePath = "/extensions") {
    const next: FilterUpdate = { ...filters.value, ...partial }
    if (!("page" in partial)) next.page = undefined
    const params = serializeFilters(next)
    const qs = params.toString()
    const path = localePath(basePath)
    return qs ? `${path}?${qs}` : path
  }

  return { filters, update, hrefForFilters }
}
```

For the admin/approvals page, you could reuse `useFilters()` directly or roll a smaller variant that only handles tier/subCat/productLineId (no pagination, search, etc.). The pattern is: `computed filters` reads route.query, `update()` calls `router.replace()` with serialized params.

export default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {
  const user = await getSessionUser(event)
  if (!user) return { isSuperAdmin: false, isReviewer: false }
  const db = useDb()
  const [superAdmin, cells] = await Promise.all([
    isSuperAdmin(db, user.id),
    listCellsForUser(db, user.id),
  ])
  return {
    isSuperAdmin: superAdmin,
    isReviewer: superAdmin || cells.length > 0,
  }
})
```

Currently returns only two booleans (`isSuperAdmin`, `isReviewer`). It does **not** expose the viewer's reviewer cells. To build smart pickers, the queue page would need to either:

- Or call a separate endpoint to fetch the user's cells directly

- `filters.queue.tierLabel` (or reuse `filters.tierLabel`)
- `filters.queue.subCatLabel`
- `admin.approvals.filters.subtitle` (optional filter section header)

## Summary

The approvals queue is primed for filtering:
- Page template has a clear mounting point (between header and table)
- Endpoint currently accepts only `view` query param; adding `tier`, `subCat`, `productLineId` filters requires shallow changes to `ListApprovalsQuerySchema`
- Orchestrator `listReviewerQueue` already computes reviewer cells; filter intersection on that array is clean
- Repository `listPendingForCells` already handles cell-array filtering; narrowing that array pre-filters elegantly
- OfficialTierPicker pattern (popover + computed active state + `update()` calls) is reusable, though you might roll a lighter variant for the admin context
- `useFilters()` manages URL state; could be reused or minimized
- Current `admin/me` endpoint lacks cell exposure—extend it if you want smart pickers; otherwise query cells separately
- FUNC_TAXONOMY is the exclusive subCat source
- i18n keys exist for tier/productLine; add subCat-specific keys as needed

## Approved Plan:
# Plan: Approvals queue filtering

## Context

After PR #43 a single reviewer can sit on a lot of cells — e.g. a
Wireless-product-line admin who covers all four product lines for a
subCat owns four `(tier × subCat × productLine)` cells, and a
super-admin sees every pending request across 45 cells. The current
`/admin/approvals` queue renders them undifferentiated in
`createdAt DESC` order. Triage becomes "scroll and pattern-match the
tier / subCat / productLine pills" on each row.

This plan adds a small pill-rail above the queue table with two
pickers — Official (tier + productLine, ported verbatim from the
listing rail) and Category (subCat) — so reviewers can narrow the
queue to one cell or one dimension at a time. URL-state-backed, so
`/en/admin/approvals?tier=productLine&productLineId=wireless` is a
shareable triage view.

User decisions implicit in the recommendation:
- **Filter dimensions**: tier, subCat, productLine. All three are
  what the cell key carries, so they're the natural narrows.
- **Picker affordance**: reuse the same Popover-trigger pill style
  the listing rail already uses; one new SubCat picker; the existing
  OfficialTierPicker drops in unchanged.
- **Smart pickers**: a non-super reviewer's pickers list only the
  options they actually cover (so a reviewer with cells only in
  `cloud` doesn't see `network`/`embedded`/etc. as live options).
  Super-admins see the full grid.

## Server side

### Validator (`shared/validators/approvals.ts`)

`ListApprovalsQuerySchema` gains three optional fields, mirroring the
existing reuse of `OfficialTier`, `SubCatKey`, and `ProductLineId`:

```ts
export const ListApprovalsQuerySchema = z.object({
  view: z.enum(["mine", "queue"]).default("mine"),
  tier: OfficialTier.optional(),
  subCat: SubCatKey.optional(),
  productLineId: ProductLineId.optional(),
})
```

No iff-rule between `tier` and `productLineId` here: the queue page
should be able to narrow to "any Wireless requests across all
subCats" (productLineId only) without forcing the user to pick tier.
The orchestrator does the right thing regardless.

### Orchestrator (`server/utils/approvals.ts`)

`listReviewerQueue` widens to `(userId, filters?)`. The filter
intersection happens **on the cells array**, before
`listPendingForCells`:

```ts
export interface ReviewerQueueFilters {
  tier?: OfficialTier
  subCat?: string
  productLineId?: string
}

export async function listReviewerQueue(
  userId: string,
  filters: ReviewerQueueFilters = {},
): Promise<approvalsRepo.ApprovalRequestRow[]> {
  // ... existing cells-from-matrix / cells-for-user fork
  const narrowed = cells.filter((c) => {
    if (filters.tier && c.tier !== filters.tier) return false
    if (filters.subCat && c.subCat !== filters.subCat) return false
    if (filters.productLineId && c.productLineId !== filters.productLineId)
      return false
    return true
  })
  return approvalsRepo.listPendingForCells(db, narrowed)
}
```

Repository `listPendingForCells` already handles an empty cells array
(returns `[]`), so a filter that excludes every cell yields an empty
queue naturally — no special-case branch.

### Endpoint (`server/api/internal/approvals/list.get.ts`)

```ts
if (query.view === "queue") {
  return {
    ok: true,
    requests: await listReviewerQueue(user.id, {
      tier: query.tier,
      subCat: query.subCat,
      productLineId: query.productLineId,
    }),
  }
}
```

`listPublisherRequests` is unaffected.

### `admin/me` exposes covered cells

`server/api/internal/admin/me.get.ts` already calls
`listCellsForUser` and uses its length. Return the array itself so the
queue page can render smart pickers:

```ts
return {
  isSuperAdmin: superAdmin,
  isReviewer: superAdmin || cells.length > 0,
  cells,  // ReviewerCell[] — empty for anonymous (we already short-circuit above)
}
```

`ReviewerCell` is already typed in `server/repositories/reviewers.ts`
as `{ tier, subCat, productLineId: string | null }`.

## UI

### `app/components/filters/SubCatPicker.vue` (new)

Mirrors `OfficialTierPicker.vue` shape — Popover + trigger reading
"Category: {value}", popover content with "All" + one option per
subCat. Reads/writes `filters.value.subCat` via `useFilters()`.

Smart options:
- Takes optional `allowedSubCats?: readonly string[]` prop. When
  provided, the picker shows only those subCats (plus "All"); when
  omitted, it falls back to `SUB_CAT_KEY_LIST` (the full 9). The page
  passes the reviewer's covered subCats; super-admin omits the prop.
- Trigger label uses the existing `taxonomy.l1.<key>` i18n keys for
  the value chunk and a new `filters.subCatPicker.triggerLabel` for
  the prefix ("Category" / "分类").

### Queue page (`app/pages/admin/approvals/index.vue`)

- Add `useFetch("/api/internal/admin/me", ...)` (with `default()`)
  alongside the existing two fetches so the smart-picker bounds and
  the super-admin grant are both in scope.
- Mount a thin `<div class="mb-4 flex flex-wrap gap-2">` between the
  header and the queue, containing `<OfficialTierPicker />` and the
  new `<SubCatPicker :allowed-sub-cats="..." />`.
- The `useFetch` on `/api/internal/approvals/list` reads the same
  three query params off `route.query` so any picker change triggers a
  refresh.

OfficialTierPicker is mounted **unchanged** — it already reads/writes
the same URL keys via `useFilters`. (The picker's lazy productLine
fetch fires regardless of which page it's on; the
`/api/internal/product-lines` endpoint is the same one the queue
page already fetches.)

### `ReviewerQueueTable.vue` (unchanged)

Already renders tier / subCat / productLine pills per row. The filter
rail above just narrows what rows are in `rows`.

## i18n keys (en + zh)

- `filters.subCatPicker.triggerLabel` — "Category" / "分类"
- `filters.subCat.all` — "All categories" / "全部分类"

The trigger reuses `taxonomy.l1.<key>` for the value; no new
per-subCat keys needed.

## Tests

- `server/utils/approvals.test.ts` — extend the existing
  `describe("listReviewerQueue")` block:
  - filters narrow the cells passed into `listPendingForCells`
  - empty-intersection (filter excludes all viewer cells) returns
    `[]` without throwing
  - super-admin path applies the same filter against the matrix-wide
    cell set
- e2e SSR (`tests/e2e/approval.spec.ts`) — anonymous load of
  `/en/admin/approvals?subCat=cloud` redirects (auth-gated). Skip a
  positive SSR assertion; the gated multi-actor block can pick up a
  picker click in a follow-up.
- Component test (optional) for `SubCatPicker.vue` — the
  `allowedSubCats` prop trims the options, "All" clears `subCat`.

## Documentation

- ADR-0001 — no change. This is a UX refinement, not an architectural
  decision.
- `docs/features.md` — one bullet under the approval-workflow section.
- `docs/daily-log.md` — fresh entry (EN + ZH).

- `shared/validators/approvals.ts` — `ListApprovalsQuerySchema` widens
- `server/utils/approvals.ts` — `listReviewerQueue` takes optional

- `server/api/internal/approvals/list.get.ts` — passes filters through
- `server/api/internal/admin/me.get.ts` — exposes `cells`

Returns\n// an empty array when the user has no cell assignments (and is not a\n// super-admin); super-admins see the whole pending queue.\nexport async function listReviewerQueue(\n  userId: string,\n): Promise<approvalsRepo.ApprovalRequestRow[]> {\n  const db = useDb()\n  if (await reviewersRepo.isSuperAdmin(db, userId)) {\n    // Treat super-admin as \"assigned to every cell\". Pulled from the matrix\n    // verbatim so an empty matrix still surfaces no rows — better than a\n    // silent firehose. Productline IS NULL is encoded as the literal '∅' in\n    // the dedup key so a (company, cloud, null) cell doesn't collapse onto\n    // (productLine, cloud, '') by accident.\n    const cells = await reviewersRepo\n      .listMatrix(db)\n      .then((rows) =>\n        Array.from(\n          new Set(\n            rows.map((r) => `${r.tier}:${r.subCat}:${r.productLineId ?? \"∅\"}`),\n          ),\n        ).map((k) => {\n          const [tier, subCat, pl] = k.split(\":\") as [OfficialTier, string, string]\n          return {\n            tier,\n            subCat,\n            productLineId: pl === \"∅\" ? null : pl,\n          }\n        }),\n      )\n    return approvalsRepo.listPendingForCells(db, cells)\n  }\n\n  const cells = await reviewersRepo.listCellsForUser(db, userId)\n  return approvalsRepo.listPendingForCells(db, cells)\n}",
  "new_string": "export interface ReviewerQueueFilters {\n  tier?: OfficialTier\n  subCat?: string\n  productLineId?: string\n}\n\n// Reviewer queue — pending requests in any cell this user covers. Returns\n// an empty array when the user has no cell assignments (and is not a\n// super-admin); super-admins see the whole pending queue.\n//\n// Optional `filters` narrow the queue without changing the trust model:\n// the cells are computed first (so a reviewer never queries outside their\n// own assignment), then filtered, then handed to listPendingForCells. A\n// filter that excludes every cell yields an empty `cells` array, which\n// listPendingForCells short-circuits to [] — no special-case branch.\nexport async function listReviewerQueue(\n  userId: string,\n  filters: ReviewerQueueFilters = {},\n): Promise<approvalsRepo.ApprovalRequestRow[]> {\n  const db = useDb()\n  let cells: Array<{\n    tier: OfficialTier\n    subCat: string\n    productLineId: string | null\n  }>\n  if (await reviewersRepo.isSuperAdmin(db, userId)) {\n    // Treat super-admin as \"assigned to every cell\". Pulled from the matrix\n    // verbatim so an empty matrix still surfaces no rows — better than a\n    // silent firehose. Productline IS NULL is encoded as the literal '∅' in\n    // the dedup key so a (company, cloud, null) cell doesn't collapse onto\n    // (productLine, cloud, '') by accident.\n    cells = await reviewersRepo\n      .listMatrix(db)\n      .then((rows) =>\n        Array.from(\n          new Set(\n            rows.map((r) => `${r.tier}:${r.subCat}:${r.productLineId ?? \"∅\"}`),\n          ),\n        ).map((k) => {\n          const [tier, subCat, pl] = k.split(\":\") as [OfficialTier, string, string]\n          return {\n            tier,\n            subCat,\n            productLineId: pl === \"∅\" ? null : pl,\n          }\n        }),\n      )\n  } else {\n    cells = await reviewersRepo.listCellsForUser(db, userId)\n  }\n\n  const narrowed = cells.filter((c) => {\n    if (filters.tier && c.tier !== filters.tier) return false\n    if (filters.subCat && c.subCat !== filters.subCat) return false\n    if (filters.productLineId && c.productLineId !== filters.productLineId)\n      return false\n    return true\n  })\n  return approvalsRepo.listPendingForCells(db, narrowed)\n}"
}

  "new_string": "// Returns safe defaults for anonymous callers rather than 401, because\n// the detail page renders for anonymous browsers too and needs to read\n// this endpoint without bailing out — the gates on the actual admin\n// pages still throw 401 separately. `cells` is returned alongside the\n// role booleans so the approvals queue page can render smart pickers\n// bounded to what the viewer actually covers; an empty array means \"no\n// cells\" rather than \"any cell allowed\".\nexport default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {\n  const user = await getSessionUser(event)\n  if (!user) {\n    return { isSuperAdmin: false, isReviewer: false, cells: [] }\n  }\n  const db = useDb()\n  const [superAdmin, cells] = await Promise.all([\n    isSuperAdmin(db, user.id),\n    listCellsForUser(db, user.id),\n  ])\n  return {\n    isSuperAdmin: superAdmin,\n    isReviewer: superAdmin || cells.length > 0,\n    cells,\n  }\n})"
}

22

24	
25	// useState dedups the fetch across other consumers (publish dialog) and

27	// that doing this once per session is the right grain.
28	const productLines = useState<ProductLine[]>("productLines", () => [])
29	const productLinesLoaded = useState<boolean>("productLines:loaded", () => false)
30	
31	async function ensureProductLines() {
32	  if (productLinesLoaded.value) return

39	  }

43	// productLine on cold load, so the trigger label can render the line
44	// name without forcing the user to open the popover.
45	watch(
46	  open,
47	  (next) => {
48	    if (next) void ensureProductLines()
49	  },

Omitting `allowedSubCats`\n// signals \"full grid\" to the picker.\nconst allowedSubCats = computed<readonly string[] | undefined>(() => {\n  if (adminMe.value.isSuperAdmin) return undefined\n  return Array.from(new Set(adminMe.value.cells.map((c) => c.subCat)))\n})\n</script>\n\n<template>\n  <div class=\"px-6 py-8 max-w-5xl mx-auto\">\n    <header class=\"mb-6\">\n      <h1 class=\"font-serif text-3xl tracking-tight text-(--color-ink)\">\n        {{ t(\"admin.approvals.title\") }}\n      </h1>\n      <p class=\"mt-1 text-sm text-(--color-ink-muted)\">\n        {{ t(\"admin.approvals.subtitle\") }}\n      </p>\n    </header>\n\n    <div class=\"mb-4 flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2\">\n      <OfficialTierPicker />\n      <SubCatPicker :allowed-sub-cats=\"allowedSubCats\" />\n    </div>\n\n    <p v-if=\"pending\" class=\"text-sm text-(--color-ink-muted)\">\n      {{ t(\"admin.approvals.loading\") }}\n    </p>\n    <ReviewerQueueTable\n      v-else\n      :rows=\"rows\"\n      :product-lines=\"productLines\"\n      @refresh=\"refresh\"\n    />\n  </div>\n</template>\n"

This results in a misleading UX where users see options that will return empty results.

## Findings Report: Extension Category Dimension for Approval Reviewer Matrix

### 1. Extension Category Enum — Confirmed Four Values

**File:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/shared/db/schema/extension.ts`

Lines 29–34:
```typescript

  "skills",
  "mcp",
  "slash",
  "plugins",
]);
```

Column definition at line 100:
```typescript
category: extensionCategoryEnum().notNull(),
```

Confirmed: **exactly four values** (skills, mcp, slash, plugins). The column is required on every extension record.

---

### 2. Approval Cell Shape Today

**Reviewer Cell Type:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/server/repositories/reviewers.ts`, lines 40–44:
```typescript
export interface ReviewerCell {
  tier: OfficialTier
  subCat: string
  productLineId: string | null
}
```

**Approval Reviewers Table:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/shared/db/schema/approval.ts`, lines 74–115:
```typescript
export const approvalReviewers = pgTable(
  "approval_reviewers",
  {
    id: text().primaryKey(),
    tier: officialTierEnum().notNull(),
    subCat: text().notNull(),
    productLineId: text().references(() => productLines.id, {
      onDelete: "restrict",
    }),
    userId: text()
      .notNull()
      .references(() => users.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
    createdAt: timestamp({ withTimezone: true }).notNull().defaultNow(),
  },
  (t) => [
    uniqueIndex("approval_reviewers_pl_cell_user_uq")
      .on(t.tier, t.subCat, t.productLineId, t.userId)
      .where(sql`tier = 'productLine'`),
    uniqueIndex("approval_reviewers_co_cell_user_uq")
      .on(t.tier, t.subCat, t.userId)
      .where(sql`tier = 'company'`),
    index("idx_approval_reviewers_cell").on(
      t.tier,
      t.subCat,
      t.productLineId,
    ),
    check(
      "approval_reviewers_pl_shape_chk",
      sql`(tier = 'productLine' AND product_line_id IS NOT NULL)
        OR (tier = 'company' AND product_line_id IS NULL)`,
    ),
  ],
);
```

**CHECK Constraint Shape:**
- Product-Line tier: `(tier = 'productLine' AND product_line_id IS NOT NULL)`
- Company tier: `(tier = 'company' AND product_line_id IS NULL)`

For a category dimension, you'd add `category` to the tier-aware unique indexes and extend the CHECK to become a three-part iff-rule: `(tier, subCat, productLineId?, category)`.

---

### 3. Approval Requests Snapshot — Category via Foreign Key

**File:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/shared/db/schema/approval.ts`, lines 22–72:

```typescript
export const approvalRequests = pgTable(
  "approval_requests",
  {
    id: text().primaryKey(),
    extensionId: text()
      .notNull()
      .references(() => extensions.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
    requestedTier: officialTierEnum().notNull(),
    subCat: text().notNull(),
    productLineId: text().references(() => productLines.id, {
      onDelete: "restrict",
    }),
    requestedByUserId: text()
      .notNull()
      .references(() => users.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
    reason: text(),
    status: approvalStatusEnum().notNull().default("pending"),
    decidedByUserId: text().references(() => users.id, {
      onDelete: "set null",
    }),
    decidedAt: timestamp({ withTimezone: true }),
    reviewerNote: text(),
    createdAt: timestamp({ withTimezone: true }).notNull().defaultNow(),
    updatedAt: timestamp({ withTimezone: true }).notNull().defaultNow(),
  },
  // ... CHECK constraint ...
);
```

**Answer:** The table does **NOT** carry a `category` column. It is implicit via the `extensionId` foreign key — you must join to `extensions.category` when you need it. The columns are: `id, extensionId, requestedTier, subCat, productLineId, requestedByUserId, reason, status, decidedByUserId, decidedAt, reviewerNote, createdAt, updatedAt`.

### 4. Submit-Request Flow — No Current Category Lookup

**File:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/server/utils/approvals.ts`, lines 50–109:

```typescript
export async function submitRequest(
  params: SubmitParams,
): Promise<approvalsRepo.ApprovalRequestRow> {
  // Shape rule mirrors the DB CHECK...
  if (params.requestedTier === "productLine" && !params.productLineId) {
    throw new ApprovalError("missing_product_line")
  }
  if (params.requestedTier === "company" && params.productLineId) {
    throw new ApprovalError("unexpected_product_line")
  }

  const db = useDb()

  const ext = await extensionsRepo.findById(db, params.extensionId)
  if (!ext) throw new ApprovalError("extension_not_found")
  if (ext.publisherUserId !== params.userId) {
    throw new ApprovalError("not_publisher_owner")
  }
  if (ext.visibility !== "published") {
    throw new ApprovalError("extension_not_published")
  }

  const row = await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
    const existing = await approvalsRepo.findPendingByExtension(
      tx,
      params.extensionId,
    )
    if (existing) throw new ApprovalError("duplicate_pending_request")

    return approvalsRepo.insertRequest(tx, {
      id: crypto.randomUUID(),
      extensionId: params.extensionId,
      requestedTier: params.requestedTier,
      subCat: params.subCat,
      productLineId: params.productLineId,
      requestedByUserId: params.userId,
      reason: params.reason ?? null,
    })
  })
  // ... Inngest event ...
  return row
}
```

**Answer:** Currently **no category lookup**. The extension is loaded at line 65 (`findById`) to validate publisher ownership and visibility. If you add a category dimension to the cell key, this is where you'd access `ext.category` (already available after line 65) and thread it into the Inngest event (line 96–106). The cell key would become `{tier, subCat, productLineId?, category}`.

---

### 5. Decide-Request Flow — Reviewer Authorization Call Site

**File:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/server/utils/approvals.ts`, lines 117–140:

```typescript
export async function decideRequest(
  params: DecideParams,
): Promise<approvalsRepo.ApprovalRequestRow> {
  const db = useDb()

  const current = await approvalsRepo.findById(db, params.requestId)
  if (!current) throw new ApprovalError("request_not_found")
  if (current.status !== "pending") {
    throw new ApprovalError("request_not_pending")
  }

  // Super-admins can decide on any cell; otherwise the reviewer must be
  // assigned to the exact (requestedTier, subCat, productLineId?) cell this
  // request was filed against. Tier mismatches don't leak across cells.
  const allowed =
    (await reviewersRepo.isSuperAdmin(db, params.reviewerUserId)) ||
    (await approvalsRepo.isReviewerForCell(
      db,
      params.reviewerUserId,
      current.requestedTier,
      current.subCat,
      current.productLineId,
    ))
  if (!allowed) throw new ApprovalError("not_reviewer")
  // ...
}
```

**Call site:** Lines 132–139. The `isReviewerForCell` call currently passes 4 args: `(db, userId, tier, subCat, productLineId)`. With a category dimension, you'd add a 5th arg. To pass the category, you'd need to load `ext.category` via a join from `current.extensionId` (as `approval_requests` lacks a category column), then pass it as `current.category` or retrieve it fresh.

---

### 6. Seed Data Shape — 45 Company Rows, 36 Product-Line Rows (9 × 4)

**File:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/shared/data/approval-reviewers.ts`, lines 14–54:

```typescript

**Count:** 9 subCats × 4 product lines × 1 reviewer per cell = 36 product-line rows. Then 9 company-tier rows. **Total: 45 seeded reviewer assignments**.

**Flatmap Pattern:** The `.flatMap((pl) => [...])` at line 23 already fans across all 4 product lines. To fan out per category (4 values), you'd nest an additional `.flatMap((cat) => [...])` or extend the outer structure to generate `(tier, subCat, productLineId?, category, reviewerEmail)` tuples. Current entries map 1:1 to cells; with categories, each would become 4 entries (or you'd use a different strategy like per-tier/per-subCat defaults that inherit across categories).

---

### 7. Matrix UI Components — 3 Approval Matrix Files

**File:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/app/components/approvals/`

Components that touch the matrix:
1. **ReviewerMatrix.vue** — Tabbed shell over company and product-line tiers.
2. **ReviewerMatrixCompany.vue** — Company-tier matrix (subCat × admin).
3. **ReviewerMatrixProductLine.vue** — Product-line-tier grid (subCat × productLine).

**Also relevant:**
- **ReviewerQueueTable.vue** — Reviewer's queue list.
- **RequestOfficialDialog.vue** — Publisher's approval request submission form.
- **RevokeTierDialog.vue** — Super-admin revocation dialog.

**Headcount:** 3 core matrix components. Adding a category dimension would affect layout (expanding each cell into a subcategory group or introducing a new nesting level, or a new tab/toggle). The UI strategy depends on your design preference — whether categories are presented as separate matrix tabs, nested rows within each (tier, subCat) cell, or a collapsed/expandable tree.

---

### 8. i18n Naming Pattern

**Taxonomy labels live at:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/i18n/locales/en.json`

**Filter keys — lines 158–192:**

**Answer:** Following the pattern, a new approval-matrix category dimension would nest under `admin.approvals.reviewers` (e.g., `admin.approvals.reviewers.category.*`) or reuse the existing `extensions.category.*` keys since they already label the four values. The existing keys `extensions.category.skills`, `extensions.category.mcp`, `extensions.category.slash`, `extensions.category.plugins` provide ready-made UI labels.

## Summary

- **Extension categories:** 4 exact values (skills, mcp, slash, plugins) in the `extension_category` enum.
- **Current cell shape:** `(tier, subCat, productLineId?)` with iff-rule CHECK constraint; adding category would expand to `(tier, subCat, productLineId?, category)` and require a 3-part iff-rule for product-line vs. company scoping.
- **Approval requests:** Don't store category; it's implicit via `extensionId` FK. You'd join to `extensions.category` when needed.
- **Submit flow:** Loads extension at line 65; category already available. Would thread `ext.category` into event and cell-key assembly.
- **Decide flow:** Call site at lines 132–139; `isReviewerForCell` would gain a 5th arg (category).
- **Seed data:** 45 rows (9 subCats × 1 company + 9 × 4 product-line). Flatmap pattern is extensible to fan per category (4× expansion = 180–360 rows depending on strategy).
- **UI:** 3 core matrix components (ReviewerMatrix, ReviewerMatrixCompany, ReviewerMatrixProductLine); design choice needed for layout (tabs, nested, tree).
- **i18n:** Pattern is `taxonomy.l1.*` for subCats, `filters.subCat.*` for filter UI. Existing `extensions.category.*` labels already cover skills/mcp/slash/plugins, so reuse them or create `admin.approvals.reviewers.category.*` aliases if you want approval-specific phrasing.

## Where the repo is

- Branch: `main`, synced with merge commit `8bf8104` (PR #45 — approvals queue filtering).
- Latest three PRs merged in this run:
  - **#43** — product-line dimension (matrix becomes `tier × subCat × productLine?`), filter rail picker, seed credentials.
  - **#44** — tier revocation (Official → Unofficial, super-admin only, from the detail page).
  - **#45** — approvals queue filtering (Official + Category pickers above the queue table, smart-bound to viewer cells via `admin/me`).
- ADR-0001 carries two dated addenda already (2026-06-08 product-line, 2026-06-09 tier-revocation).
- `bun run validate` passes at 36 files / 360 tests.

## Required pre-reads (in order)

1. **`CLAUDE.md`** — particularly locked decision #12 (workflow shape), the workflow section (commit per coherent unit, pause before push, no `--no-verify`, no Co-Authored-By trailer), and the "Dev sign-in" line.
2. **`docs/adr/0001-official-tier-approval-workflow.md`** — both the original four locked decisions AND the two addenda. Reuse the addendum format if you write a third.
3. **`docs/plan.md` §3** — current schema state for `approval_reviewers`, `approval_requests`, `extensions`, `product_lines`.

## The proposed task

User asked: "add an administrator configuration matrix page to assign approval administrators across functional categories, corporate levels, and product lines, **configured separately by extension type**."

Decoding: the matrix already keys on `tier × subCat × productLine?`. The user wants to add **`extensions.category`** (`skills | mcp | slash | plugins`) as a fourth axis, so each cell splits four ways — different admins for Skills vs MCP vs Slash vs Plugins inside the same `(tier, subCat, productLine?)` cell. Routing for a submitted request reads `extensions.category` to pick the right admin.

## Two open clarifying questions

These need user answers before drafting a plan. Pose them with `AskUserQuestion`. Recommendations in parentheses are my read; the user has the call.

1. **Migration strategy for existing reviewer assignments.**
   - Fan out each existing row × 4 categories (recommended — same approach as PR #43's productLine fan-out: 45 seed rows → 180, admins drop the categories they don't want via the matrix UI).
   - Default to `skills`-only and require re-assignment for MCP / Slash / Plugins (cleaner data, much louder break — three quarters of the queue goes empty).
   - Wipe and re-seed (cleanest schema, biggest UX disruption).

2. **Where the category axis sits in `/admin/reviewers` UI.**
   - Top-level extension-type tab row above the existing Company / Product-Line tier tabs (recommended — smallest UI change, preserves the existing mental model, pattern matches the listing-rail filter affordance).
   - A category column inside each existing grid (denser, harder to scan).
   - Four independent `/admin/reviewers/<category>` routes (heavyweight).

Other design choices the planner can decide directly without asking:
- Snapshot `category` on `approval_requests` (matches the existing pattern where `subCat` and `productLineId` are snapshotted from the extension at submit time — even though they're derivable via the FK).
- `category` is NOT NULL on both `approval_reviewers` and `approval_requests`. No iff-rule; category is always required for every cell, unlike productLineId.
- The publisher's submit dialog (`RequestOfficialDialog.vue`) does **not** need a category picker — `extensions.category` is fixed; the orchestrator reads it after `extensionsRepo.findById`.
- The admin/me `cells` field added in PR #45 needs to grow a `category` member so the queue page's smart pickers stay correct.
